sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十二】起重光大荒落，盡旃蒙作噩，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 52] From Chongguang Dahuangluo through Zhanmeng Zuo'e, altogether five years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 52] Spanning from Chongguang Dahuangluo through Zhanmeng Zuo'e—a period of five years in all.

translations.literal: The eleventh year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultured (
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元八零一年）

translations.literal: xinsi, 801 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinsi, 801 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅，韓全義至長安，竇文場為掩其敗跡，上禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, Han Quanyi arrived at Chang'an; Dou Wenchang covered up his defeat for him, and the emperor treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day jiayin of the first month, Han Quanyi reached Chang'an. Dou Wenchang concealed the record of his defeat, and the emperor received him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 全義稱足疾，不任朝謁，遣司馬崔放入對。

translations.literal: Quanyi claimed foot ailment and could not attend court audience; he sent his staff officer Cui Fang to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi pleaded foot trouble and declined court audience, dispatching his staff officer Cui Fang to respond in his stead.

sentences.zh: 放為全義引咎，謝無功，上曰：「全義為招討使，能招來少誠，其功大矣，何必殺人然後為功邪！」

translations.literal: Fang took blame on Quanyi's behalf and apologized for achieving no merit. The emperor said, "As pacification commissioner, Quanyi was able to win over Shaocheng—his merit is great. Why must one kill people before it counts as merit!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang accepted blame for Quanyi and apologized for their lack of success. The emperor said, "As pacification commissioner, Quanyi was able to win over Shaocheng—his achievement is considerable. Must merit always be measured by how many are killed?"

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲戌，歸夏州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiaxu, he returned to Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiaxu, Quanyi returned to Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韋士宗既入黔州，妄殺將吏，人心大擾。

translations.literal: After Wei Shizong had entered Qian Prefecture, he wantonly killed officers and clerks, and popular sentiment was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Shizong had taken up office in Qian Prefecture, he killed officers and clerks without cause, throwing the region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 士宗懼，三月，脫身亡走。

translations.literal: Shizong grew afraid; in the third month he slipped away and fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Shizong fled in the third month.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，以右諫議大夫裴佶為黔州觀察使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinhai, Right Remonstrance Censor Pei Ji was appointed observation commissioner of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on xinhai of the fourth month, Right Remonstrance Censor Pei Ji was appointed observation commissioner of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day renxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon renxu, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 朔方邠、寧，慶節度使楊朝晟防秋於寧州，乙酉，薨。

translations.literal: Yang Chaosheng, military governor of Shuofang, Bin, Ning, and Qing, was on autumn defense at Ning Prefecture; on yiyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaosheng, military governor of Shuofang, Bin, Ning, and Qing, was stationed on autumn defense at Ning Prefecture; on yiyou he died.

sentences.zh: 初，渾瑊遣兵馬使李朝寀將兵戌定平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hun Jian had sent army-and-horse commissioner Li Chaocai to lead troops garrisoning Dingping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hun Jian had dispatched army-and-horse commissioner Li Chaocai to garrison Dingping with troops.

sentences.zh: 瑊薨，朝寀請以其眾隸神策軍；

translations.literal: When Jian died, Chaocai requested that his force be attached to the Shence Army;
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's death, Chaocai asked that his troops be placed under the Shence Army;

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 楊朝晟疾亟，召僚佐謂曰：「朝晟必不起，朔方命帥多自本軍，雖徇眾情，殊非國體。

translations.literal: Yang Chaosheng's illness grew critical; he summoned his staff and said, "Chaosheng will certainly not recover. Appointing commanders for Shuofang mostly from within that army may satisfy the troops' wishes, but it is quite contrary to the proper order of the state.
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Chaosheng's illness turned grave, he summoned his staff and said, "I shall not rise again. When Shuofang commanders are chosen from within the same army, the troops may be pleased, but it is poor policy for the realm.

sentences.zh: 寧州刺史劉南金，練習軍旅，宜使攝行軍，且知軍事，比朝遷擇帥，必無虞矣。」

translations.literal: Liu Nanjin, prefect of Ning Prefecture, is practiced in military affairs; he should be made acting commander of the army and placed in charge of military affairs. By the time the court selects a commander, there will surely be no trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nanjin, prefect of Ning Prefecture, is skilled in military affairs. Let him act as commander of the army and manage military affairs. By the time the court appoints a permanent commander, all will be secure."

sentences.zh: 又以手書授監軍劉英倩，英倩以聞。

translations.literal: He also handed a letter in his own hand to army supervisor Liu Yingqian, and Yingqian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave a letter in his own hand to army supervisor Liu Yingqian, who reported it upstream.

sentences.zh: 軍士私議曰：「朝廷命帥，吾納之，即命劉君，吾事之；

translations.literal: The soldiers privately discussed among themselves, saying, "If the court appoints a commander, we will accept him; if it appoints Lord Liu, we will serve him;
translations.idiomatic: The men whispered among themselves: "If the court names a commander, we will accept him; if it names Lord Liu, we will follow him;

sentences.zh: 若命帥於它軍，彼必以其麾下來，吾屬被斥矣，必拒之。」

translations.literal: but if a commander is appointed from another army, he will surely bring his own followers, and we will be cast aside—we must resist."
translations.idiomatic: but if the commander comes from another army, he will bring his own men and cast us aside—we must refuse."

sentences.zh: 己丑，上遣中使往察軍情，軍中多與南金。

translations.literal: On jichou the emperor sent a palace envoy to investigate army sentiment; most in the army favored Nanjin.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the emperor sent a palace envoy to sound out the army; most favored Nanjin.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上復遺高品薛盈珍繼詔詣寧州。

translations.literal: On xinmao the emperor again sent the high-ranking eunuch Xue Yingzhen with a follow-up edict to Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he sent the senior eunuch Xue Yingzhen again with a supplementary edict to Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲午，盈珍至軍，宣詔曰：「朝寀所將本朔方軍，今將並之，以壯軍勢，威戎狄，以李朝寀為使，南金副之，軍中以為何如？」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiawu, Yingzhen reached the army and proclaimed the edict: "The troops Chaocai leads are originally from the Shuofang army; they will now be merged to strengthen military power and overawe the barbarians. Li Chaocai is to be commander with Nanjin as deputy—what does the army think of this?"
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiawu, Yingzhen arrived and proclaimed: "The force Chaocai commands is originally from Shuofang; it will now be merged to strengthen the army and awe the frontier peoples. Li Chaocai shall be commander and Nanjin deputy—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆奉詔。

translations.literal: All the generals accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 丙申，都虞候史經言於眾曰：「李公命收弓刀而送甲冑二千。」

translations.literal: On bingshen, chief adjutant Shi Jing said to the assembly, "Lord Li has ordered bows and blades collected and two thousand suits of armor sent."
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen chief adjutant Shi Jing told the troops, "Lord Li has ordered your bows and blades taken and two thousand suits of armor delivered up."

sentences.zh: 軍士皆曰：「李公欲內麾下二千為腹心，吾輩妻子其可保乎！」

translations.literal: The soldiers all said, "Lord Li means to bring in two thousand of his own men as his inner guard—how can our wives and children be safe!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cried, "Lord Li wants to bring in two thousand of his own men as a personal guard—what becomes of our families!"

sentences.zh: 夜，造劉南金，欲奉以為帥，南金曰：「節度使固我所欲，然非天子之命則不可，軍中豈無它將乎！

translations.literal: That night they went to Liu Nanjin, wishing to install him as commander. Nanjin said, "To be military governor is indeed what I want, but without the Son of Heaven's command it cannot be done. Is there no other general in the army!
translations.idiomatic: That night they sought out Liu Nanjin to make him commander. Nanjin said, "I would gladly be military governor, but not without the Son of Heaven's appointment. Is there no other officer in this army?

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「弓刀皆為官所收，惟軍事府尚有甲兵，欲因以集事。

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Bows and blades have all been taken by the authorities; only the military affairs office still has armor and weapons—we wish to use them to carry out our plan."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "The authorities have seized our bows and blades; only the military affairs office still holds armor and arms—we mean to use them to act."

sentences.zh: 南金曰：「諸君不願朝寀為帥，宜以情告敕使。

translations.literal: Nanjin said, "If you gentlemen do not wish Chaocai as commander, you should explain your feelings to the edict envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjin said, "If you will not have Chaocai as commander, tell the edict envoy plainly.

sentences.zh: 若操甲兵，乃拒詔也。」

translations.literal: If you take up arms, that is defying an edict."
translations.idiomatic: To seize arms would be to defy the throne."

sentences.zh: 命閉門不內。

translations.literal: He ordered the gates shut and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his gates and refused them entry.

sentences.zh: 軍士去，詣兵馬使高固，固逃匿，搜得之。

translations.literal: The soldiers left and went to army-and-horse commissioner Gao Gu; Gu hid himself, but they searched him out.
translations.idiomatic: They left and went to army-and-horse commissioner Gao Gu, who hid himself until they found him.

sentences.zh: 固曰：「諸君能用吾命則可。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "If you gentlemen will obey my orders, it can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "If you will obey my commands, it may be done."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「惟命。」

translations.literal: The crowd said, "We await your word."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We await your word."

sentences.zh: 固曰：「毋殺人，毋掠金帛。」

translations.literal: Gu said, "Do not kill, do not plunder gold and silk."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "Do not kill, do not plunder gold or silk."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 乃共詣監軍，請奏之。

translations.literal: Then together they went to the army supervisor and asked that he report it.
translations.idiomatic: Together they went to the army supervisor and asked him to report upstream.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「劉君既得朝旨為副帥，必撓吾事。」

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Lord Liu, having received the court's order as deputy commander, will surely thwart our affair."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Lord Liu, now deputy commander by court order, will surely obstruct us."

sentences.zh: 詐稱監軍命，召計事，至而殺之。

translations.literal: They falsely claimed an order from the army supervisor, summoned him to discuss affairs, and when he arrived killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Feigning an order from the army supervisor, they summoned him on business and killed him when he came.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，制以李朝寀為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: On wuxu an imperial appointment made Li Chaocai military governor of Bin and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Li Chaocai was appointed military governor of Bin and Ning by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 是日，寧州告變者至，上追還制書，復遣薛盈珍往詗軍情。

translations.literal: That day word of mutiny at Ning Prefecture arrived; the emperor recalled the appointment and again sent Xue Yingzhen to investigate army sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: That day news of mutiny at Ning arrived; the emperor recalled the appointment and sent Xue Yingzhen again to probe the army.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，至軍，軍中以高固為請，盈珍即以上旨命固知軍事。

translations.literal: On renyin he reached the army; the army asked for Gao Gu, and Yingzhen immediately appointed Gu to manage military affairs by imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he reached the camp; the troops asked for Gao Gu, and Yingzhen at once appointed Gu to manage military affairs by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 或傳戊戌制書至邠州，邠軍惑，不知所從。

translations.literal: Some reported that the wuxu appointment had reached Bin Prefecture; the Bin army was confused and did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the wuxu appointment reached Bin Prefecture; the Bin troops were unsettled and unsure whom to obey.

sentences.zh: 奸人乘之，且為變。

translations.literal: Evildoers seized the opportunity and were about to stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers seized the moment and were ready to rise.

sentences.zh: 留後孟子周悉內精甲於府廷，日饗士卒，內以悅眾心，外以威奸黨。

translations.literal: Acting prefect Meng Zizhou secretly stationed elite armor in the prefectural courtyard, feasted the soldiers daily, inwardly to please the troops and outwardly to overawe the schemers.
translations.idiomatic: Acting prefect Meng Zizhou secretly posted elite armor in the government compound and feasted the troops daily—winning their hearts within while cowing plotters without.

sentences.zh: 邠軍無變，子周之謀也。

translations.literal: The Bin army did not mutiny—this was Zizhou's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin army did not rise; this was Zizhou's doing.

sentences.zh: 李錡既執天下利權，以貢獻固主恩，以饋遺結權貴，恃此驕縱，無所忌憚，盜取縣官財，所部官屬無罪受戮者相繼。

translations.literal: Li Qi, having seized control of the empire's profit rights, used tribute to secure imperial favor and gifts to bind powerful men; relying on this he grew arrogant and unrestrained, fearing nothing, stole government funds, and among his subordinates innocent men were executed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi had seized the empire's revenue streams, using tribute to secure the emperor's favor and gifts to bind the powerful. Emboldened, he grew reckless, stole state funds, and put innocent subordinates to death in succession.

sentences.zh: 浙西布衣崔善貞詣闕上封事，言宮市、進奉及鹽鐵之弊，因言錡不法事。

translations.literal: A commoner of western Zhe, Cui Shanzhen, came to the capital with a sealed memorial denouncing abuses of the palace market, tribute deliveries, and the salt-and-iron monopoly, and also reported Qi's illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shanzhen, a commoner of western Zhe, submitted a sealed memorial at court on abuses of the palace market, tribute levies, and the salt-and-iron monopoly, and also denounced Qi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 上覽之，不悅，命械送錡。

translations.literal: The emperor read it, was displeased, and ordered Shanzhen sent in fetters to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with displeasure and ordered Shanzhen sent in chains to Qi.

sentences.zh: 錡聞其將至，先鑿坑於道旁。

translations.literal: When Qi heard he was coming, he first dug a pit by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he was on his way, Qi had a pit dug beside the road.

sentences.zh: 己亥，善貞至，並鎖械內坑中，生瘞之。

translations.literal: On jihai Shanzhen arrived; they locked him in fetters, placed him in the pit, and buried him alive.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Shanzhen arrived; they shackled him, cast him into the pit, and buried him alive.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞之，不寒而慄。

translations.literal: When far and near heard of it, men shuddered without cold.
translations.idiomatic: News of it made men shudder across the land.

sentences.zh: 錡復欲為自全計，增廣兵眾，選有材力善射者謂之挽強，胡、奚雜類謂之蕃落，給賜十倍它卒。

translations.literal: Qi again sought to secure himself, enlarged his forces, selected men of strength skilled in archery and called them "Draw-the-Strong," and mixed Hu and Xi tribesmen he called "Frontier Settlers," granting them ten times other soldiers' pay.
translations.idiomatic: Qi again sought his own safety, expanded his troops, chose strong archers as "Draw-the-Strong," and enrolled mixed Hu and Xi as "Frontier Settlers," paying them ten times ordinary soldiers.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官盧坦屢諫不悛，與幕傣李約等皆去之。

translations.literal: Transportation judge Lu Tan remonstrated repeatedly without effect and left with staff members Li Yue and others.
translations.idiomatic: Transportation judge Lu Tan remonstrated in vain and departed with secretariat staff Li Yue and others.

sentences.zh: 約，勉之子也。

translations.literal: Yue was the son of Li Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was a son of Li Mian.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以高固為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: On jiyou Gao Gu was appointed military governor of Bin and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Gao Gu was appointed military governor of Bin and Ning.

sentences.zh: 固，宿將，以寬厚得眾，節度使忌之，置於散地，同列多輕侮之；

translations.literal: Gu was a veteran general who had won the troops through generosity; the military governor had envied him and placed him in an idle post, and his peers often slighted him;
translations.idiomatic: Gu was a veteran who had won the army through kindness; a military governor had envied him and kept him in a sinecure, and colleagues often looked down on him;

sentences.zh: 及起為帥，一無所報復，由是軍中遂安。

translations.literal: when he rose to command he took no revenge at all, and thereby the army was soon at peace.
translations.idiomatic: yet once he became commander he exacted no revenge, and the army soon settled.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，成德節度使王武俊薨。

translations.literal: On dingsi Wang Wujun, military governor of Chengde, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Wang Wujun, military governor of Chengde, died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，吐蕃寇鹽州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Tibet raided Salt Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on wuyin of the seventh month, Tibet raided Salt Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以成德節度副使王士真為節度使。

translations.literal: On xinsi Wang Shizhen, deputy military governor of Chengde, was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Wang Shizhen, Chengde's deputy military governor, was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 己丑，吐蕃陷麟州，殺刺史郭鋒，夷其城郭，掠居人及党項部落而去。

translations.literal: On jichou Tibet took Lin Prefecture, killed prefect Guo Feng, razed the walls, and carried off inhabitants and Tangut tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Tibet captured Lin Prefecture, killed Prefect Guo Feng, razed the city, and carried off residents and Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 鋒，曜之子也。

translations.literal: Feng was a son of Guo Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was a son of Guo Yao.

sentences.zh: 僧延素為虜所得。

translations.literal: The monk Yansu was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Yansu was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 虜將有徐舍人者，謂延素曰：「我英公之五代孫也。

translations.literal: Among the captors was a retainer named Xu who said to Yansu, "I am the fifth-generation descendant of Lord Ying.
translations.idiomatic: A captor, Retainer Xu, told Yansu, "I am the fifth-generation descendant of Lord Ying.

sentences.zh: 武後時，吾高祖建義不成，子孫流播異域，雖代居祿位典兵，然思本之心不忘，顧宗族大，無由自撥耳。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time my great-grandfather raised arms but failed; his descendants were scattered to foreign lands. Though we have held office and commanded troops for generations, the heart that yearns for our roots has not been forgotten—but the clan is too large to extricate ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu my ancestor rose in arms and failed; our line was scattered abroad. Though we have held rank and commanded troops for generations, we have never forgotten our origins—yet our clan is too large to break free.

sentences.zh: 今聽汝歸。」

translations.literal: Today I release you to return."
translations.idiomatic: Today I release you to go home."

sentences.zh: 遂縱之。

translations.literal: He then let him go.
translations.idiomatic: And he let him go.

sentences.zh: 上遣使敕韋皋出兵深入吐蕃以分其勢，紓北邊患。

translations.literal: The emperor sent orders to Wei Gao to lead troops deep into Tibet to divide their strength and ease the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wei Gao to strike deep into Tibet to divide their strength and relieve the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 皋遣將將兵二萬分出九道，攻吐蕃維、保、松州及棲雞、老翁城。

translations.literal: Gao sent generals with twenty thousand men in nine columns to attack Tibetan Wei, Bao, and Song prefectures and the strongpoints Qiji and Laoweng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent generals with twenty thousand men in nine columns against Tibetan Wei, Bao, and Song prefectures and the strongpoints Qiji and Laoweng.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使鄭儋暴薨，不及命後事，軍中喧嘩，將有它變。

translations.literal: Zheng Dan, military governor of Hedong, died suddenly without leaving orders for succession; the army clamored and was about to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dan, military governor of Hedong, died suddenly without arranging succession; the army roared and was near mutiny.

sentences.zh: 中夜，十餘騎執兵召掌書記令狐楚至軍門，諸將環之，使草遺表。

translations.literal: At midnight more than ten horsemen with weapons summoned chief secretary Linghu Chu to the army gate; the generals surrounded him and made him draft a final memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a dozen horsemen with weapons summoned chief secretary Linghu Chu to the gate; the generals ringed him and made him draft the death memorial.

sentences.zh: 楚在白刃之中，操筆立成。

translations.literal: Chu, amid naked blades, took brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: Amid naked blades Chu took brush and finished on the spot.

sentences.zh: 楚，德棻之族也。

translations.literal: Chu was of the clan of Linghu Defen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu belonged to the clan of Linghu Defen.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，以河東行軍司馬嚴綬為節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, Yan Shou, marching army supervisor of Hedong, was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuwu, Hedong marching army supervisor Yan Shou was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 九月，韋皋奏大破吐蕃於雅州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wei Gao reported a great defeat of Tibet at Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wei Gao reported a great defeat of Tibet at Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 左神策中尉竇文場致仕，以副使楊志廉代之。

translations.literal: Palace army supervisor Dou Wenchang retired; his deputy Yang Zhiqian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wenchang, chief of the Left Shence Army, retired; deputy Yang Zhiqian replaced him.

sentences.zh: 韋皋屢破吐蕃，轉戰千里，凡撥城七，軍鎮五，焚堡百五十，斬首萬餘級，捕虜六千，降戶三千，遂圍維州及昆明城。

translations.literal: Wei Gao repeatedly defeated Tibet, campaigning a thousand li; in all he took seven cities, five garrisons, and burned a hundred fifty forts, beheaded more than ten thousand, captured six thousand, received three thousand surrendering households, and then besieged Wei Prefecture and Kunming city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao repeatedly defeated Tibet in campaigns of a thousand li: seven cities taken, five garrisons, a hundred fifty forts burned, more than ten thousand heads, six thousand captives, three thousand households who surrendered—and then he besieged Wei Prefecture and Kunming.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚子，加皋檢校司徒兼中書令，賜爵南康王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengzi, Gao was made acting Minister of Works and concurrently Grand Councillor, and granted the title Prince of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on gengzi of the tenth month, Gao was made acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor and created Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 南詔王異牟尋虜獲尤多，上遣中使慰撫之。

translations.literal: The Nanzhao king Yi Mouxun had taken many captives; the emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: King Yi Mouxun of Nanzhao had taken many captives; the emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 戊午，鹽州剌史杜彥先棄城奔慶州。

translations.literal: On wuwu Salt Prefecture prefect Du Yanxian abandoned the city and fled to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Salt Prefecture prefect Du Yanxian abandoned his post and fled to Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十一貞元十八年（

translations.literal: The twelfth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultured (
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元八零二年）

translations.literal: renwu, 802 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renwu, 802 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，驃己摩羅思那遣其子悉利移入貢。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, King Pyusaw Hti of Pyu sent his son Prince Siliyi to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first month, King Pyusaw Hti of Pyu sent his son Siliyi to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 驃國在南詔西南六千八百里，聞南詔內附而慕之。

translations.literal: Pyu lies sixty-eight hundred li southwest of Nanzhao; hearing that Nanzhao had submitted within, it admired the court.
translations.idiomatic: Pyu lay sixty-eight hundred li southwest of Nanzhao; learning that Nanzhao had submitted to the Tang, it admired the court.

sentences.zh: 因南詔入見，仍獻其樂。

translations.literal: It entered audience through Nanzhao and also presented its music.
translations.idiomatic: It came to court by way of Nanzhao and presented its music as well.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣其大相兼東鄙五道節度使論莽熱將兵十萬解維州之圍，西川兵據險設伏以待之。

translations.literal: Tibet sent its chief minister and eastern frontier five-circuit military governor Lun Mangre with a hundred thousand men to relieve the siege of Wei Prefecture; Western Shu troops held the passes and set ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent chief minister and eastern frontier commander Lun Mangre with a hundred thousand men to lift the siege of Wei; Western Shu troops held the defiles in ambush.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃至，出千人挑戰，虜悉眾追之，伏發，虜眾大敗，擒論莽熱，士卒死者太半。

translations.literal: When Tibet arrived, a thousand men came out to challenge; the barbarians pursued with their full force, the ambush struck, and the enemy army was routed; Lun Mangre was captured and more than half the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans came, a thousand men sallied to challenge them; the enemy pursued in full force, the ambush sprang, and the host was shattered—Lun Mangre captured and more than half the army dead.

sentences.zh: 維州、昆明竟不下，引兵還。

translations.literal: Wei Prefecture and Kunming could not be taken; they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Kunming still would not fall; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，皋遣使獻論莽熱，上赦之。

translations.literal: On yihai Gao sent envoys presenting Lun Mangre; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Gao sent envoys presenting Lun Mangre; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 浙樂觀察使裴肅既以進奉得進，判官齊總代掌後務，刻剝以求媚又過之。

translations.literal: Pei Su, observation commissioner of Zhexi, had advanced through tribute offerings; after he left, judge Qi Zong managed affairs and extorted the people to curry favor even more ruthlessly than before.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Su of Zhexi observation had risen through tribute; when he left, judge Qi Zong ran affairs and squeezed the people for favor even harder.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸酉，詔擢總為衢州剌史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guiyou, an edict promoted Zong to prefect of Qu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guiyou, an edict promoted Zong to prefect of Qu.

sentences.zh: 給事中長安許孟容封還詔書，曰：「衢州無它虞，齊總無殊績，忽此超獎，深駭群情。

translations.literal: Chief draftsman Xu Mengrong of Chang'an returned the edict, saying, "Qu Prefecture has no special concerns; Qi Zong has no outstanding merit. This sudden reward deeply alarms public sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting officer Xu Mengrong of Chang'an returned the edict, saying, "Qu has no special need; Zong has no notable achievement. This sudden promotion shocks all who hear it.

sentences.zh: 若總必有可錄，願明書勞課，然後超資改官，以解眾疑。」

translations.literal: If Zong truly has merit to record, let his labors be stated plainly, and then let him be promoted beyond his rank to quiet doubt."
translations.idiomatic: If Zong truly deserves reward, let his service be written out plainly—then promote him beyond rank and quiet the doubts."

sentences.zh: 詔遂留中。

translations.literal: The edict was therefore held at court.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was held at court.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上召孟容，慰獎之。

translations.literal: On jihai the emperor summoned Mengrong and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the emperor summoned Mengrong and praised him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，嘉王府咨議高弘本正牙奏事，自理逋債。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinwei, Gao Hongben, adviser to the Prince of Jia's household, presented himself at regular court audience to report a private matter and collect debts owed him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on xinwei of the seventh month, adviser Gao Hongben of the Prince of Jia's household came to regular court audience to press a private debt.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔「公卿庶僚自今勿令正牙奏事，如有陳秦，宜延英門請對。」

translations.literal: On yihai an edict said, "From today ministers and officials are not to present matters at regular court audience; if they have petitions, they should request audience at the Yanying Gate."
translations.idiomatic: On yihai an edict declared, "Hereafter ministers and officials shall not present business at regular audience; petitions should be made at audience before the Yanying Gate."

sentences.zh: 議者以為：「正牙奏事，自武德以來未之或改，所以達群情，講政事。

translations.literal: Commentators held that presenting matters at regular court audience had not been changed since the Wude era, for the purpose of conveying public sentiment and discussing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators argued that regular court audience had stood unchanged since the Wude reign as the channel for public sentiment and state business.

sentences.zh: 弘本無知，黜之可也，不當因人而廢事。」

translations.literal: Hongben was ignorant; dismissing him would suffice—it should not mean abolishing the institution because of one man."
translations.idiomatic: Hongben was simply ignorant; dismiss him—but do not abolish the institution for one man's sake."

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使杜佑累表求代。

translations.literal: Du You, military governor of Huainan, repeatedly memorialized asking to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, military governor of Huainan, repeatedly asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁亥，以刑部尚書王鍔為淮南副節度使兼行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dinghai, Minister of Justice Wang E was made deputy military governor of Huainan and concurrently marching army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on dinghai of the tenth month, Minister of Justice Wang E was appointed deputy military governor of Huainan and marching army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 己酉，鄜坊節度使王棲曜薨。

translations.literal: On jiyou Wang Qiyao, military governor of Fufang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Wang Qiyao, military governor of Fufang, died.

sentences.zh: 中軍將何朝宗謀作亂，夜，縱火。

translations.literal: Central army commander He Chaozong plotted rebellion; at night he set fires.
translations.idiomatic: Central army commander He Chaozong plotted mutiny and set fires by night.

sentences.zh: 都虞候裴玢潛匿不救火，旦，擒朝宗，斬之。

translations.literal: Chief adjutant Pei Bin hid himself and did not fight the fire; at dawn he seized Chaozong and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief adjutant Pei Bin held back from fighting the blaze; at dawn he seized Chaozong and executed him.

sentences.zh: 以同州刺史劉公濟為鄜坊節度使，以玢為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Liu Gongji, prefect of Tong Prefecture, was made military governor of Fufang, and Bin was made marching army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongji of Tong Prefecture became military governor of Fufang; Pei Bin became marching army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十一貞元十九年（

translations.literal: The thirteenth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultured (
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元八零三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, 803 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guiwei, 803 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，丁亥，名安黃軍曰奉義。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on dinghai, the Anhuang army was named Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on dinghai of the second month, the Anhuang army was renamed Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 己亥，安南牙將王季元逐其觀察使裴泰，泰奔朱鳶。

translations.literal: On jihai Wang Jiyuan, a junior officer of Annan, drove out his observation commissioner Pei Tai; Tai fled to Zhuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Wang Jiyuan, a junior officer of Annan, expelled observation commissioner Pei Tai, who fled to Zhuyuan.

sentences.zh: 明日，左兵馬使趙勻斬季元及其黨，迎泰而復之。

translations.literal: The next day Left Army-and-Horse Commissioner Zhao Yun beheaded Jiyuan and his partisans and welcomed Tai back to office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Left Army-and-Horse Commissioner Zhao Yun killed Jiyuan and his faction and restored Tai.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，杜佑入朝。

translations.literal: On jiachen Du You entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Du You came to court.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬子朔，以佑檢校司空、同平章事；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the new moon renzi, You was made acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon renzi, You was made acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor;

sentences.zh: 以王鍔為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Wang E was made military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E was made military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿王權請遷獻、懿二祖於德明、興聖廟，每禘祫，正太祖東向之位；

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Wang Quan asked to move the two ancestors Xian and Yi to the temples of Deming and Xingsheng, and at each di and xia sacrifice to set the founding ancestor in the east-facing position;
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Entertainments director Wang Quan asked to move ancestors Xian and Yi to the temples of Deming and Xingsheng and, at each di and xia sacrifice, to seat the founding ancestor facing east;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以司農卿李實兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: On yihai Minister of Agriculture Li Shi was made concurrent metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Minister of Agriculture Li Shi was also made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 實為政暴戾，上愛信之。

translations.literal: Shi governed with violence and cruelty, yet the emperor loved and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi ruled with cruelty, yet the emperor favored and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 實恃恩驕傲，許人薦引，不次拜官，及誣譖斥逐，皆如期而效，士大夫畏之側目。

translations.literal: Relying on favor he grew arrogant, promised men recommendations and out-of-turn appointments, and when he slandered and expelled others it all came to pass as he said—scholar-officials feared him and averted their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by favor, he promised promotions and out-of-turn appointments, and his slanders and expulsions always took effect on schedule—officials feared him and looked away.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，涇原節度使劉昌奏請徙原州治平涼，從之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Chang, military governor of Jingyuan, memorialized asking to move the seat of Yuan Prefecture to Pingliang; it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Jingyuan military governor Liu Chang asked to move Yuan Prefecture's seat to Pingliang; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吐蕃遣其臣論頰熱入貢。

translations.literal: On yihai Tibet sent its minister Lun Binre to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Tibet sent minister Lun Binre with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛卯，以右神策中尉副使孫榮義為中尉，與楊志廉皆驕縱招權，依附者眾，宦官之勢益盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinmao, Right Shence deputy army supervisor Sun Rongyi was made chief army supervisor; he and Yang Zhiqian were both arrogant and grasped power, and with many adherents eunuch power grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinmao, Sun Rongyi became Right Shence chief supervisor; he and Yang Zhiqian both grew arrogant and gathered power, and with many followers eunuch influence swelled further.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，遣右龍武大將軍薛伾使於吐蕃。

translations.literal: On renchen the Right Dragon Martial general Xue Pi was sent as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Right Dragon Martial general Xue Pi was dispatched to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 陳許節度使上官兌薨，其婿田偁欲脅其子使襲軍政。

translations.literal: Shangguan Dui, military governor of Chenxu, died; his son-in-law Tian Chen wished to coerce Dui's son into seizing military government.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu military governor Shangguan Dui died; his son-in-law Tian Chen tried to force Dui's son to seize control of the army.

sentences.zh: 牙將王沛，亦兌之婿也，知其謀，以告監軍范日用，討擒之。

translations.literal: Junior officer Wang Pei, also Dui's son-in-law, learned of the plot and told army supervisor Fan Riyong, who attacked and captured Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Junior officer Wang Pei, another son-in-law of Dui, learned of the plot, informed army supervisor Fan Riyong, and Chen was seized.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以陳許行軍司馬劉昌裔為節度使。

translations.literal: On yiwei Liu Changyi, marching army supervisor of Chenxu, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Chenxu marching army supervisor Liu Changyi was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 沛，許州人也。

translations.literal: Pei was a man of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was from Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自正月不雨至於秋七月。

translations.literal: From the first month there was no rain until the seventh month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: No rain fell from the first month until the seventh month of autumn.

sentences.zh: 己未，中書侍郎、同平章事齊抗以疾罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On jiwei Vice Grand Councillor Qi Kang was removed for illness and made tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Vice Grand Councillor Qi Kang, ill, was made tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，翰林待詔王伾善書，山陰王叔文善棋，俱出入東宮，娛侍太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hanlin attendant Wang Pi was skilled at calligraphy and Shanyin Wang Shuwen skilled at chess; both went in and out of the Eastern Palace to entertain the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hanlin attendant Wang Pi excelled at calligraphy and Shanyin's Wang Shuwen at chess; both attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 伾，杭州人也。

translations.literal: Pi was a man of Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was from Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 叔文譎詭多計，自言讀書知治道，乘間常為太子言民間疾苦。

translations.literal: Shuwen was crafty and full of schemes; he claimed that through reading he knew the way of governance, and whenever he had opportunity he told the crown prince of the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was cunning and scheming, claiming his studies had taught him statecraft; he often told the crown prince of popular suffering when he could.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗與諸侍讀及叔文等論及宮市事，太子曰：「寡人方欲極言之。」

translations.literal: The crown prince once discussed the palace market with his tutors and Shuwen and others; the crown prince said, "I am about to speak out fully on this."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once discussed the palace market with his tutors and Shuwen; he said, "I mean to speak out fully on this."

sentences.zh: 眾皆稱讚，獨叔文無言。

translations.literal: All praised him, but Shuwen alone was silent.
translations.idiomatic: All praised the idea; only Shuwen said nothing.

sentences.zh: 既退，太子自留叔文，謂曰：「向者君獨無言，豈有意邪？」

translations.literal: After they withdrew the crown prince kept Shuwen and said, "Just now you alone were silent—did you have some thought?"
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew the crown prince kept Shuwen and asked, "You alone were silent—did you have some reservation?"

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「叔文蒙幸太子，有所見，敢不以聞？

translations.literal: Shuwen said, "Shuwen has been favored by the crown prince; if I have a view, how dare I not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen said, "Having the crown prince's favor, how could I withhold my view?

sentences.zh: 太子職當視膳問安，不宜言外事。

translations.literal: The crown prince's duty is to attend to meals and inquire after health; he should not speak of outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A crown prince's duty is to attend his father's meals and health; he should not discuss outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下在位久，如疑太子收人心，何以自解！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has reigned long; if he suspects the crown prince is winning hearts, how can you explain yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has reigned long; if he suspects you are winning hearts, how will you answer!"

sentences.zh: 太子大驚，因泣曰：「非先生，寡人無以知此。」

translations.literal: The crown prince was greatly alarmed and wept, saying, "Without you, sir, I would never have known this."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was shaken and wept: "Without you, I would never have understood this."

sentences.zh: 逐大愛幸，與王伾相依附。

translations.literal: He thereupon favored Shuwen greatly and relied on Wang Pi.
translations.idiomatic: He then favored Shuwen deeply and clung to Wang Pi.

sentences.zh: 叔文因為太子言：「某可為相，某可為將，幸異日用之。」

translations.literal: Shuwen therefore told the crown prince, "So-and-so can be chancellor, so-and-so can be a general—please employ them when the day comes."
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen told the crown prince, "This man can be chancellor, that one a general—remember them for later."

sentences.zh: 密結翰林學士韋執誼及當時朝士有名而求速進者陸淳、呂溫、李景儉、韓曄、韓泰、陳諫、柳宗元、劉禹錫等，定為死友。

translations.literal: He secretly joined Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi and such court men of reputation seeking rapid advancement as Lu Chun, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and others, fixing them as sworn friends unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly bound Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi and ambitious courtiers—Lu Chun, Lü Wen, Li Jingjian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Chen Jian, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and others—as sworn allies.

sentences.zh: 而凌准、程異等又因其黨以進，日與游處，蹤跡詭秘，莫有知其端者。

translations.literal: Ling Zhun, Cheng Yi, and others also advanced through this faction; day by day they associated together, their tracks secret—no one knew their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zhun, Cheng Yi, and others rose through the same circle; they met daily in secret, and none knew their design.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮或陰進資幣，與之相結。

translations.literal: Military governors sometimes sent gifts in secret to join with them.
translations.idiomatic: Some governors secretly sent them gifts to win their favor.

sentences.zh: 淳，吳人，嘗為左司郎中；

translations.literal: Chun was a man of Wu and had served as Left Department director;
translations.idiomatic: Chun, a man of Wu, had been Left Department director;

sentences.zh: 溫，渭之子，時為左拾遣；

translations.literal: Wen was the son of Wei and was then Left Remembrancer;
translations.idiomatic: Wen, son of Lü Wei, was then Left Remembrancer;

sentences.zh: 景儉，濡之孫，進士及第；

translations.literal: Jingjian was the grandson of Li Ru and had passed the jinshi examination;
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian, grandson of Li Ru, was a jinshi graduate;

sentences.zh: 曄，滉之族子；

translations.literal: Ye was a clansman of Han Huang;
translations.idiomatic: Ye was of Han Huang's clan;

sentences.zh: 諫，嘗為待御史；

translations.literal: Jian had served as attendant censor;
translations.idiomatic: Jian had been attendant censor;

sentences.zh: 宗元、禹錫，時為監察御史。

translations.literal: Zongyuan and Yuxi were then surveillance censors.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan and Yuxi were surveillance censors.

sentences.zh: 左補闕張正一上書，得召見。

translations.literal: Left Supplementation Censor Zhang Zhengyi submitted a memorial and was granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: Left Supplementation Censor Zhang Zhengyi memorialized and was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 正一與吏部員外郎王仲舒、主客員外郎劉伯芻等相親善，叔文之黨疑正一言己陰事，令韋執誼反譖正一等於上，雲其朋黨，游宴無度。

translations.literal: Zhengyi was close to Wang Zhongshu, outer director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Liu Bochu, outer director of the Ministry of Rites, and others; Shuwen's faction suspected Zhengyi had spoken of their secret affairs and had Wei Zhiyi slander Zhengyi and the rest to the emperor, saying they formed a clique and feasted without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyi was intimate with Personnel outer director Wang Zhongshu and Rites outer director Liu Bochu; Shuwen's faction feared he had betrayed their secrets and had Wei Zhiyi accuse them to the throne of forming a clique and dissolute feasting.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，正一等皆坐遠貶，人莫知其由。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiayin, Zhengyi and the rest were all banished far away, and no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin, Zhengyi and the others were exiled to distant posts, and none knew the reason.

sentences.zh: 伯芻，乃之子也。

translations.literal: Bochu was a son of Nai.
translations.idiomatic: Bochu was a son of Liu Nai.

sentences.zh: 鹽夏節度判官崔文先權知鹽州，為政苛刻。

translations.literal: Cui Wenxian, judge of the Yanxia circuit, held acting authority over Salt Prefecture and governed harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxia circuit judge Cui Wenxian acted for Salt Prefecture and ruled with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 冬，閏十月，庚戌，部將李庭俊作亂，殺而臠食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the intercalary tenth month, on gengxu, officer Li Tingjun mutinied, killed Wenxian, and dismembered and ate his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on gengxu of the intercalary tenth month, officer Li Tingjun mutinied, killed Wenxian, and dismembered and ate him.

sentences.zh: 左神策兵馬使李興幹戍鹽州，殺庭俊以聞。

translations.literal: Li Xinggan, army-and-horse commissioner of the Left Shence Army garrisoning Salt Prefecture, killed Tingjun and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Left Shence army-and-horse commissioner Li Xinggan, garrisoning Salt, killed Tingjun and reported upstream.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，門下侍郎、同平章事崔損薨。

translations.literal: On dingsi Vice Grand Councillor Cui Sun died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Vice Grand Councillor Cui Sun died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅朔，以李興幹為鹽州刺史，得專奏事，自是鹽州不隸夏州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the new moon wuyin, Li Xinggan was made prefect of Salt Prefecture with the right to memorialize directly; from this Salt Prefecture was no longer subordinate to Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon wuyin, Li Xinggan became prefect of Salt with direct memorial rights; Salt was thereafter detached from Xia.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申，以太常卿高郢為中書侍郎，吏部侍郎鄭珣瑜為門下侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, Director of Imperial Sacrifices Gao Ying was made Vice Grand Councillor, and Vice Minister of Personnel Zheng Xunyu was made Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat; both were Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengshen, Gao Ying became Vice Grand Councillor and Zheng Xunyu Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat—both Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜，餘慶之從父兄弟也。

translations.literal: Xunyu was a cousin of Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu was a cousin of Zheng Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 建中初，敕京城諸使及府縣系囚，每季終委御史巡案，有冤濫者以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era an edict ordered that prisoners held by capital agencies and prefectures and counties be inspected each quarter-end by censors, and any wrongful or excessive cases reported.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, an edict required quarterly censor inspection of prisoners held by capital agencies and local governments, with wrongful cases reported.

sentences.zh: 近歲，北軍移牒而已。

translations.literal: In recent years the northern armies merely sent transfer documents.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the northern armies merely forwarded transfer notices.

sentences.zh: 監察御史崔薳遇下嚴察，下吏欲陷之，引以入右神策軍。

translations.literal: Surveillance censor Cui Yuan, while investigating after court dismissal, was framed by subordinate clerks who had him taken into the Right Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance censor Cui Yuan, investigating after court, was framed by clerks who had him seized into the Right Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 軍使以下駭懼，具奏其狀。

translations.literal: The army supervisors and below were terrified and fully reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisors below were alarmed and reported the full circumstances.

sentences.zh: 上怒，杖薳四十，流崖州。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, had Yuan beaten forty strokes, and exiled him to Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger had Yuan beaten forty strokes and exiled him to Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹嗣道王實務徵求以給進奉，言於上曰：「今歲雖旱而禾苗甚美。」

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Prince of Sidao Wang Shi, pressed collections to supply tribute offerings and said to the emperor, "Though this year is drought-stricken, the grain shoots are very fine."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao metropolitan prefect Prince of Sidao Wang Shi squeezed collections for tribute and told the emperor, "Though the year is drought-stricken, the grain looks excellent."

sentences.zh: 由是租稅皆水免，人窮至壞屋賣瓦木、麥苗以輸官。

translations.literal: Thereupon all land tax was remitted on grounds of flood, yet the people were so destitute they tore down houses to sell tiles and timbers and sold wheat seedlings to pay the government.
translations.idiomatic: On that pretext all land tax was remitted for flood, yet people were so poor they demolished houses for tiles and timber and sold wheat seedlings to pay the state.

sentences.zh: 優人成輔端為謠嘲之。

translations.literal: The actor Cheng Fuduan made a ballad mocking him.
translations.idiomatic: The actor Cheng Fuduan sang a lampoon of him.

sentences.zh: 實奏輔端誹謗朝政，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Shi memorialized that Fuduan had slandered court policy and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shi reported that Fuduan had slandered court policy and had him clubbed to death.

sentences.zh: 監察御史韓愈上疏，以「京畿百姓窮困，應今年稅錢及草粟等征未得者，請俟來年蠶麥。」

translations.literal: Surveillance censor Han Yu submitted a memorial stating, "The people of the capital region are destitute; for this year's tax money and fodder grain and other levies not yet collected, I ask that collection wait until next year's silkworm and wheat harvest."
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance censor Han Yu memorialized that the capital people were destitute and asked that uncollected taxes, fodder, and grain wait until the next silkworm and wheat season.

sentences.zh: 愈坐貶陽山令。

translations.literal: Yu was demoted to magistrate of Yangshan for this.
translations.idiomatic: For this Yu was demoted to magistrate of Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十一貞元二十年（

translations.literal: The fourteenth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultured (
translations.idiomatic: The fourteenth year of Zhenyuan of Emperor Dezong (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元八零四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, 804 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiashen, 804 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙戌，天德軍都防禦團練使、豐州刺史李景略卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on bingxu, Li Jinglue, commander of the Tiande defense and training corps and prefect of Feng Prefecture, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on bingxu of the first month, Tiande commander and Feng Prefecture prefect Li Jinglue died.

sentences.zh: 初，景略嘗宴僚佐，行酒者誤以醯進。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jinglue once feasted his staff, the cup-bearer mistakenly presented vinegar.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Jinglue feasted his staff, the cup-bearer mistakenly served vinegar.

sentences.zh: 判官京兆任迪簡以景略性嚴，恐行酒者獲罪，強飲之，歸而嘔血。

translations.literal: Judge Ren Dijian of Jingzhao, knowing Jinglue's stern temper and fearing the cup-bearer would be punished, drank it by force and vomited blood when he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Ren Dijian of Jingzhao, knowing Jinglue's severity and fearing for the cup-bearer, forced himself to drink it and vomited blood at home.

sentences.zh: 軍士聞之泣下。

translations.literal: When the soldiers heard of it they wept.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers wept when they heard.

sentences.zh: 及李景略卒，軍士皆曰判官仁者，欲奉以為帥。

translations.literal: When Li Jinglue died the soldiers all said the judge was a man of benevolence and wished to install him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinglue died the men called the judge benevolent and wished to make him commander.

sentences.zh: 監軍抱置別室，軍士發扃取之。

translations.literal: The army supervisor held him in a separate room, but the soldiers broke the bolt and took him out.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor locked him in a side room, but the soldiers broke the bolt and took him.

sentences.zh: 監軍以聞，詔以代景略。

translations.literal: The army supervisor reported it, and an edict appointed him to replace Jinglue.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor reported it, and an edict appointed him to succeed Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普死，其弟嗣立。

translations.literal: The Tibetan king died and his younger brother succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan king died; his younger brother succeeded.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，名陳許軍曰忠武。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, the Chenxu army was named Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on bingyin of the fourth month, the Chenxu army was renamed Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍李升雲將禁軍鎮咸陽，疾病，其子政諲與虞候上官望等謀效山東籓鎮，使將士奏攝父事。

translations.literal: Left Golden Guards general Li Shengyun led imperial troops garrisoning Xianyang; when ill, his son Zhengshi and adjutant Shangguan Wang and others plotted to imitate the Shandong military governors and had the officers memorialize that the son should act for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Left Golden Guards general Li Shengyun garrisoned Xianyang with imperial troops; when ill, his son Zhengshi and adjutant Shangguan Wang plotted to copy the Shandong governors and had the troops petition for the son to act in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，升雲卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, Shengyun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Shengyun died.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔追削升雲官爵，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On jiayin an edict posthumously stripped Shengyun of rank and office and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin an edict posthumously stripped Shengyun of rank and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使李長榮薨，上遣中使以手詔授本軍大將，但軍士所附者即授之。

translations.literal: Li Changrong, military governor of Zhaoyi, died; the emperor sent a palace envoy with an imperial letter to confer it on a senior general of that army—whoever the troops followed would receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi military governor Li Changrong died; the emperor sent a palace envoy with a letter to give to whichever senior general the army favored.

sentences.zh: 時大將來希皓為眾所服，中使將以後詔付之。

translations.literal: At the time senior general Lai Xihao was trusted by the masses; the envoy was about to deliver the later edict to him.
translations.idiomatic: Senior general Lai Xihao then commanded the men's trust; the envoy was to deliver the edict to him.

sentences.zh: 希皓言於眾曰：「此軍取人，合是希皓，但作節度使不得。

translations.literal: Xihao said to the assembly, "This army chooses its man—it should be Xihao, but I cannot be military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xihao told the troops, "This army picks its leader—it ought to be me, but I cannot be military governor.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷以一束草來，希皓亦必敬事。」

translations.literal: If the court sent a bundle of straw, Xihao would still serve it respectfully."
translations.idiomatic: If the court sent a bundle of straw, I would still obey it faithfully."

sentences.zh: 中使言：「面奉進止，只令此軍取大將校與節鋮，朝廷不別除人。」

translations.literal: The envoy said, "I received orders face to face: this army alone is to choose a senior officer for the command seal; the court will not appoint anyone else."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "By direct order this army alone is to choose a senior officer for the seal; the court will appoint no outsider."

sentences.zh: 希皓固辭。

translations.literal: Xihao firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xihao firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使盧從史其位居四，潛與監軍相結，起出伍曰：「若來大夫不肯受詔，從史請且句當此軍。」

translations.literal: Army-and-horse commissioner Lu Congshi, fourth in rank, had secretly joined with the army supervisor; he stepped from the ranks and said, "If Lord Lai will not accept the edict, Congshi asks to manage this army for the time being."
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-ranked army-and-horse commissioner Lu Congshi had secretly aligned with the army supervisor; stepping forward he said, "If Lord Lai will not take the edict, let Congshi manage the army for now."

sentences.zh: 監軍曰：「盧中丞若如此，此亦固合聖旨。」

translations.literal: The army supervisor said, "If Vice Commissioner Lu does so, that too accords with the imperial intent."
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor said, "If Vice Commissioner Lu does this, it fits the imperial intent."

sentences.zh: 中使因探懷取詔以授之。

translations.literal: The envoy then reached into his robe, took out the edict, and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy drew the edict from his robe and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 從史捧詔，再拜舞蹈。

translations.literal: Congshi received the edict, bowed twice, and performed the dance of obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi received the edict, bowed twice, and performed the ritual dance.

sentences.zh: 希皓亟回揮同列，北面稱賀。

translations.literal: Xihao quickly turned and signaled his peers; facing north they offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Xihao swiftly turned to his peers; facing north they offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 軍士畢集，更無一言。

translations.literal: The soldiers all assembled and said nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The troops gathered; not another word was spoken.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，己未，詔以從史為節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on jiwei, an edict made Congshi military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on jiwei of the eighth month, Congshi was appointed military governor by edict.

sentences.zh: 九月，太子始得風疾，不能言。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the crown prince first suffered wind illness and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the crown prince fell ill with aphasia and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 順宗至德弘道大聖大安孝皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Shunzong, the Sagely Cultured, Greatly Virtuous, and Greatly Peaceful Filial
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong, the Sagely Cultured, Greatly Virtuous, and Greatly Peaceful Filial

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十一永貞元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Yongzhen of Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Sagely Cultured (
translations.idiomatic: The first year of Yongzhen of Emperor Dezong (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元八零五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, 805 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, 805 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未朔，諸王、親戚入賀德宗，太子獨以疾不能來，德宗涕泣悲歎，由是得疾，日益甚。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon xinwei, princes and kinsmen entered to congratulate Dezong; the crown prince alone, ill, could not come. Dezong wept and sighed in grief, fell ill thereby, and grew daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon xinwei of the first month, princes and kin came to congratulate Dezong; the crown prince alone, too ill to attend. Dezong wept until he fell ill himself, and worsened day by day.

sentences.zh: 凡二十餘日，中外不通，莫知兩宮安否。

translations.literal: For more than twenty days court and countryside had no communication, and none knew whether the two palaces were safe.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-odd days capital and provinces were cut off; none knew whether emperor and heir were alive.

sentences.zh: 癸已，德宗崩。

translations.literal: On guisi Dezong died.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Dezong died.

sentences.zh: 蒼猝召翰林學士鄭絪、衛次公等至金鑾殿草遺詔。

translations.literal: In haste the Hanlin academicians Zheng Qun, Wei Cigong, and others were summoned to the Jinluan Hall to draft the final edict.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Zheng Qun, Wei Cigong, and others were hurriedly summoned to Jinluan Hall to draft the death edict.

sentences.zh: 宦官或曰：「禁中議所立尚未定。」

translations.literal: Some eunuchs said, "Within the palace the choice of successor is not yet settled."
translations.idiomatic: Some eunuchs said, "The succession within the palace is not yet decided."

sentences.zh: 眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: No one dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: None dared answer.

sentences.zh: 次公遽言曰：「太子雖有疾，地居塚嫡，中外屬心。

translations.literal: Cigong spoke up at once, saying, "Though the crown prince is ill, he stands as legitimate heir, and court and country look to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong spoke up: "Though the crown prince is ill, he is the legitimate heir, and all hearts are with him.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，猶應立廣陵王。

translations.literal: If it cannot be helped, the Prince of Guangling should still be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no choice, enthroned still must be the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 不然，必大亂。」

translations.literal: Otherwise there will surely be great disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the realm will surely fall into chaos."

sentences.zh: 絪等從而和之，議始定。

translations.literal: Qun and the rest thereupon agreed, and the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qun and the others concurred, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 次公，河東人也。

translations.literal: Cigong was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 太子知人情憂疑，紫衣麻鞋，力疾出九仙門，召見諸軍使，人心粗安。

translations.literal: Knowing that people were anxious and doubtful, the crown prince wore purple robes and hemp sandals, forced himself out through the Jiuxian Gate despite illness, summoned the army commissioners, and hearts were somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the people's fear, the crown prince in purple and hemp sandals forced himself through the Jiuxian Gate, summoned the army commissioners, and unease eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，宣遺詔於宣政殿，太子縗服見百官。

translations.literal: On jiawu the death edict was proclaimed in the Xuanzheng Hall; the crown prince in mourning garb received the officials.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the death edict was proclaimed at Xuanzheng Hall; the crown prince in mourning received the officials.

sentences.zh: 丙申，即皇帝位於太極殿。

translations.literal: On bingshen he took the throne in the Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he ascended the throne in Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 衛士尚疑之，企足引領而望之，曰：「真太子也！」

translations.literal: The guards still doubted; standing on tiptoe they stretched their necks to look and said, "It is truly the crown prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Guards still doubted; craning their necks they cried, "It is truly the crown prince!"

sentences.zh: 乃喜而泣。

translations.literal: Then they rejoiced and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Then they wept for joy.

sentences.zh: 時順宗失音，不能決事，常居宮中施簾帷，獨宦官李忠言、昭容牛氏侍左右。

translations.literal: At the time Shunzong had lost his voice and could not decide affairs; he constantly dwelt within the palace behind curtain screens, with only the eunuch Li Zhongyan and Lady of Handsome Favor Niu in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had lost his voice and could not govern; he stayed behind curtains with only eunuch Li Zhongyan and Lady Niu at his side.

sentences.zh: 百官奏事，自帷中可其奏。

translations.literal: When officials memorialized, approval came from within the curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' memorials were approved from behind the curtains.

sentences.zh: 自德宗大漸，王伾先入，稱詔召王叔文，坐翰林中使決事。

translations.literal: From the time Dezong's illness grew critical, Wang Pi entered first, claiming an edict summoning Wang Shuwen; they sat in Hanlin while eunuchs decided affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong lay dying, Pi entered first, claiming an edict for Shuwen; they sat in Hanlin while eunuchs decided policy.

sentences.zh: 伾以叔文意入言於忠言，稱詔行下，外初無知者。

translations.literal: Pi conveyed Shuwen's intent to Zhongyan, and orders went out in the emperor's name; at first those outside knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Pi relayed Shuwen's wishes to Zhongyan, and edicts went forth—at first the outside world knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 以杜佑攝塚宰。

translations.literal: Du You was made acting chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was made acting chief mourner.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯，上始朝百官於紫宸門。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guimao, the emperor first held court for officials at the Zichen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guimao, the emperor first received officials at Zichen Gate.

sentences.zh: 己酉，加義武節度使張茂昭同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiyou Zhang Maozhao, military governor of Yiwu, was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Yiwu military governor Zhang Maozhao was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以吏部郎中韋執誼為尚書左丞、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinhai Wei Zhiyi, director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Personnel director Wei Zhiyi became Left Vice Minister and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 王叔文欲專國政，首引執誼為相，己用事於中，與相唱和。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen wished to monopolize state affairs; he first brought in Zhiyi as chancellor, while he himself already wielded power within and harmonized with the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen sought to monopolize government; he made Zhiyi chancellor while he himself already held inner power and worked in concert with him.

sentences.zh: 壬子，李師古發兵屯西境以脅滑州。

translations.literal: On renzi Li Shigu mobilized troops on his western border to threaten Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Li Shigu massed troops on his western border to threaten Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時告哀使未至諸道，義成牙將有自長安還得遺詔者，節度使李元素以師古鄰道，欲示無外，遣使密以遺詔示之。

translations.literal: At the time mourning envoys had not yet reached the circuits; a junior officer of Yicheng who had returned from Chang'an with the death edict—military governor Li Yuansu, wishing to show he harbored no outward designs toward Shigu's neighboring circuit, secretly sent an envoy to show him the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning envoys had not yet reached the circuits; a Yicheng officer back from Chang'an with the edict—governor Li Yuansu, to show goodwill toward neighbor Shigu, secretly showed him the edict.

sentences.zh: 師古欲乘國喪侵噬鄰境，乃集將士謂曰：「聖上萬福，而元素忽傳遺詔，是反也，宜擊之。」

translations.literal: Shigu wished to seize the national mourning to swallow neighboring territory; he assembled his officers and said, "The sage enjoys ten thousand blessings, yet Yuansu suddenly transmits a death edict—this is rebellion and should be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: Shigu meant to exploit the mourning to seize neighbor lands; he told his officers, "The emperor lives—yet Yuansu sends a death edict. That is treason; attack him."

sentences.zh: 遂杖元素使者，發兵屯曹州，且告假道於汴。

translations.literal: He thereupon beat Yuansu's envoy, mobilized troops at Cao Prefecture, and asked passage through Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Yuansu's envoy, mobilized at Cao, and asked passage through Bian.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使韓弘使謂曰：「汝能越吾界而為盜邪！

translations.literal: Xuanwu military governor Han Hong sent word, saying, "Can you cross my border to be a bandit!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu governor Han Hong said, "Will you cross my border to plunder?

sentences.zh: 有以相待，毋為空言！」

translations.literal: If you have something to offer, do not speak empty words!"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean business, do not talk emptily!"

sentences.zh: 元素告急，弘使謂曰：「吾在此，公安無恐。」

translations.literal: Yuansu reported urgency; Hong sent word, "I am here—you need not fear."
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu cried for help; Hong said, "I am here—you are safe."

sentences.zh: 或告曰：「翦棘夷道，兵且至矣，請備之。」

translations.literal: Someone reported, "They are clearing brambles and leveling the road—troops will soon arrive; please prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "They are clearing the road—troops are coming; prepare."

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「兵來，不除道也。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "When troops come, they will not clear the road."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "When troops come, they will not bother to clear the road."

sentences.zh: 不為之應。

translations.literal: He made no response to it.
translations.idiomatic: He did nothing.

sentences.zh: 師古詐窮變索，且聞上即位，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Shigu, his fraud exhausted and plans changed, and hearing that the emperor had ascended the throne, then disbanded his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu, his bluff spent and hearing of the new reign, disbanded his troops.

sentences.zh: 元素表請自貶。

translations.literal: Yuansu memorialized asking to demote himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu asked to demote himself.

sentences.zh: 朝廷兩慰解之。

translations.literal: The court comforted and reassured both men.
translations.idiomatic: The court comforted both parties.

sentences.zh: 元素，泌之族弟也。

translations.literal: Yuansu was a cousin of Li Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu was a cousin of Li Bi.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠以牛皮鞋材遺師古，師古以鹽資少誠，潛過宣武界，事覺，弘皆留，輸之庫，曰：「此於法不得以私相饋。」

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng sent Shigu leather for shoes; Shigu paid Shaocheng in salt, secretly crossing Xuanwu territory; when discovered, Hong detained everything and turned it in to the treasury, saying, "By law private gifts may not be exchanged."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng sent Shigu shoe leather; Shigu paid in salt, secretly crossing Xuanwu—Hong seized all and deposited it, saying, "The law forbids private gifts."

sentences.zh: 師古等皆憚之。

translations.literal: Shigu and the others all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu and the rest feared him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔數京兆尹道王實殘暴掊斂之罪，貶通州長史。

translations.literal: On xinyou an edict enumerated the crimes of Prince of Sidao Wang Shi, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, for cruel exactions, and demoted him to senior administrator of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict denounced Jingzhao prefect Wang Shi's cruel exactions and demoted him to senior administrator of Tong.

sentences.zh: 市裡歡呼，皆袖瓦礫遮道伺之，實由間道獲免。

translations.literal: The marketplaces shouted for joy; all tucked tiles and stones in their sleeves to block the road and wait for him, but Shi escaped by a bypath.
translations.idiomatic: Markets rejoiced; people lined the road with tiles and stones, but Shi escaped by a back route.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以殿中丞王伾為左散騎常侍，依前翰林待詔，蘇州司功王叔文為起居舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: On renxu Palace Directorate aide Wang Pi was made Left Regular Cavalry Attendant, continuing as Hanlin attendant; Suzhou registrar Wang Shuwen was made Diary Keeper and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Wang Pi became Left Regular Cavalry Attendant, still Hanlin attendant; Suzhou registrar Wang Shuwen became Diary Keeper and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 伾寢陋，吳語，上所褻狎；

translations.literal: Pi was ugly in appearance and spoke the Wu dialect; the emperor treated him with familiar intimacy;
translations.idiomatic: Pi was homely and spoke Wu dialect; the emperor treated him familiarly;

sentences.zh: 而叔文頗任事自許，微知文義，好言事，上以故稍敬之，不得如伾出入無阻。

translations.literal: Shuwen, rather self-confident in managing affairs, knew literary principles somewhat and liked to discuss policy, so the emperor therefore respected him somewhat more and did not allow him the unhindered access Pi enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was more self-assured in affairs, knew some letters, and loved policy talk—the emperor respected him somewhat but denied him Pi's free access.

sentences.zh: 叔文入至翰林，而伾入至柿林院，見李忠言、牛昭容計事。

translations.literal: Shuwen entered as far as Hanlin, while Pi entered as far as the Persimmon Grove courtyard to see Zhongyan and Lady Niu and discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen went only to Hanlin; Pi went to the Persimmon Grove to meet Zhongyan and Lady Niu.

sentences.zh: 大抵叔文依伾，伾依忠言，忠言依牛昭容，轉相交結。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, Shuwen relied on Pi, Pi on Zhongyan, Zhongyan on Lady Niu—they passed power in a chain.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen relied on Pi, Pi on Zhongyan, Zhongyan on Lady Niu—a chain of patronage.

sentences.zh: 每事先下翰林，使叔文可否，然後宣於中書，韋執誼承而行之。

translations.literal: Every affair was first sent down to Hanlin for Shuwen's approval or rejection, then proclaimed in the Secretariat, and Wei Zhiyi carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter went first to Hanlin for Shuwen's yes or no, then to the Secretariat for Zhiyi to execute.

sentences.zh: 外黨則韓泰、柳宗元、劉禹錫等主采聽外事。

translations.literal: The outer faction had Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and others gather intelligence on outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, and others gathered outside intelligence.

sentences.zh: 謀議唱和，日夜汲汲如狂，互相推獎，曰伊、曰周、曰管、曰葛，僩然自得，謂天下無人。

translations.literal: In counsel they echoed one another day and night like madmen, praising one another as Yi, Zhou, Guan, or Ge, smugly self-satisfied, thinking none under heaven their equal.
translations.idiomatic: They schemed day and night like men possessed, calling one another Yi, Zhou, Guan, or Ge, smugly sure none on earth matched them.

sentences.zh: 榮辱進退，生於造次，惟其所欲，不拘程式。

translations.literal: Honor and disgrace, advancement and dismissal, arose in a moment—whatever they wished, unconstrained by procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and ruin came at a whim—whatever they wanted, heedless of procedure.

sentences.zh: 士大夫畏之，道路以目。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials feared them; travelers averted their eyes on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Officials feared them; travelers looked away on the road.

sentences.zh: 素與往還者，相次撥擢，至一日除數人。

translations.literal: Those who had dealings with them were promoted in succession—sometimes several men in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Associates were promoted in waves—several appointments in a single day.

sentences.zh: 其黨或言曰，「某可為某官，」不過一二日，輒已得之。

translations.literal: Their faction would say, "So-and-so can hold such-and-such office," and within a day or two it was done.
translations.idiomatic: They would say, "So-and-so should have such an office," and within a day or two it was his.

sentences.zh: 於是叔文及其黨十餘家之門，晝夜車馬如市。

translations.literal: Thereupon the gates of Shuwen and his faction of more than ten households were day and night thronged with carriages and horses like a market.
translations.idiomatic: The gates of Shuwen and a dozen allied houses swarmed day and night with carriages like a market.

sentences.zh: 客候見叔文、伾者，至宿其坊中餅肆、酒壚下，一人得千錢，乃容之。

translations.literal: Clients waiting to see Shuwen or Pi would lodge overnight in cake shops and wine stalls below their lanes; one man paid a thousand cash before he was admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Clients seeking Shuwen or Pi slept in shops below their lanes and paid a thousand cash for admission.

sentences.zh: 伾尤闒茸，專以納賄為事，作大匱貯金帛，夫婦寢其上。

translations.literal: Pi was especially base, devoting himself to taking bribes; he made great chests to store gold and silk and husband and wife slept atop them.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was basest of all, living on bribes; he kept great chests of gold and silk and slept atop them with his wife.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上御丹鳳門，赦天下，諸色逋負，一切蠲免，常貢之外，悉罷進奉。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor faced the Vermilion Phoenix Gate, pardoned the empire, remitted all categories of arrears, and beyond regular tribute abolished all special presentations.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor faced Vermilion Phoenix Gate, pardoned the realm, remitted all arrears, and ended special tribute beyond regular levies.

sentences.zh: 貞元之末政事為人患者，如宮市，五坊小兒之類，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Evils of late Zhenyuan government that harmed the people, such as the palace market and the Five-Ward boys, were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Late Zhenyuan abuses—the palace market, the Five-Ward boys—were abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是五坊小兒張捕鳥雀於閭裡者，皆為暴橫以取人錢物，至有張羅網於門，不許人出入者，或張井上使不得汲者。

translations.literal: Earlier the Five-Ward boys who spread nets in lanes to catch birds were all violent and extorted people's money; some stretched nets across gates so people could not enter or exit, or across wells so people could not draw water.
translations.idiomatic: Five-Ward boys netting birds in lanes extorted money; some blocked gates or wells from use.

sentences.zh: 近之，輒曰：「汝驚供奉鳥雀！」

translations.literal: When approached they would say, "You have startled the birds for the palace!"
translations.idiomatic: If approached they cried, "You frightened the palace birds!"

sentences.zh: 即痛毆之，出錢物求謝，乃去。

translations.literal: They would beat the person severely, who paid money to apologize before they left.
translations.idiomatic: They beat the person until he paid to be released.

sentences.zh: 或相聚飲食於酒食之肆，醉飽而去，賣者或不知，就索其直，多被毆詈。

translations.literal: Or they would gather to eat and drink at food shops, eat and drink their fill and leave; the seller might not know and would ask payment and often be beaten and reviled.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted at shops and left unpaid; sellers who asked were beaten.

sentences.zh: 或時留蛇一囊為質，曰：「此蛇所以致鳥雀而捕之者，今留付汝，幸善飼之，勿令飢渴。」

translations.literal: Sometimes they left a bag of snakes as pledge, saying, "This snake is to lure and catch birds; I leave it with you—please feed it well and do not let it hunger or thirst."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they left a bag of snakes, saying, "Feed this well—it catches birds for us."

sentences.zh: 賣者愧謝求哀，乃攜挈而去。

translations.literal: The seller would apologize in shame and beg mercy before they took it away.
translations.idiomatic: Sellers apologized humbly before they took the snakes away.

sentences.zh: 上在東官，皆知其弊，故即位首禁之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was crown prince he knew these abuses, and therefore upon enthronement he first forbade them.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince he had known these abuses and banned them first upon enthronement.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，罷鹽鐵使月進錢。

translations.literal: On yichou the monthly surplus payments of the salt-and-iron commissioner were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the salt commissioner's monthly surplus payments were abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是，鹽鐵月進羨餘而經入益少，至是，罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier the salt-and-iron office's monthly surplus remittances had reduced regular revenue; now it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly surplus remittances had shrunk regular revenue; now they ended.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛未，以王伾為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinwei, Wang Pi was made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinwei, Wang Pi was made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 德宗之末，十年無赦，群臣以微過譴逐者皆不復敘用，至是始得量移。

translations.literal: At the end of Dezong's reign there had been no amnesty for ten years; officials banished for slight faults were not reemployed—now they were first allowed transfer.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years under late Dezong there had been no amnesty; the banished were now first allowed transfer.

sentences.zh: 壬申，追忠州別駕陸贄、郴州別駕鄭餘慶、杭州刺史韓皋、道州刺史陽城赴京師。

translations.literal: On renshen Lu Zhi, senior administrator of Zhong Prefecture, Zheng Yuqing, senior administrator of Chen Prefecture, Han Gao, prefect of Hang Prefecture, and Yang Cheng, prefect of Dao Prefecture, were summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Lu Zhi, Zheng Yuqing, Han Gao, and Yang Cheng were recalled to the capital.
