sentences.zh: 贄之秉政也，貶駕部員外郎李吉甫為明州長史，既而徙忠州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhi held power he had demoted Personnel outer director Li Jiji to senior administrator of Ming Prefecture, later transferring him to Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi held power he had demoted Li Jiji to Ming, later to Zhong.

sentences.zh: 贄昆弟門人鹹以為憂，至而吉甫忻然以宰相禮事之。

translations.literal: Zhi's brothers, disciples, and followers all worried; when Jiji arrived he gladly treated Zhi with chancellor's courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's kin and followers worried; Jiji received him with chancellor's courtesy.

sentences.zh: 贄初猶慚懼，後遂為深交。

translations.literal: At first Zhi was ashamed and afraid, but afterward they became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhi was ashamed, but they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 吉甫，棲筠之子。

translations.literal: Jiji was a son of Li Qijun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji was a son of Li Qijun.

sentences.zh: 韋皋在成都，屢上表請以贄自代。

translations.literal: Wei Gao at Chengdu repeatedly memorialized asking that Zhi replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao at Chengdu repeatedly asked that Zhi replace him.

sentences.zh: 贄與陽城皆未聞追詔而卒。

translations.literal: Zhi and Yang Cheng both died without hearing of the recall edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Yang Cheng both died before the recall reached them.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，加杜佑度支及諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: On bingxu Du You was given charge of revenue and salt-and-iron transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Du You was given revenue and salt transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 以浙西觀察使李錡為鎮海節度使，解其鹽轉運使。

translations.literal: Li Qi, observation commissioner of western Zhe, was made military governor of Zhenhai, relieved of salt transport duties.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhe commissioner Li Qi was made Zhenhai military governor and stripped of salt transport.

sentences.zh: 錡雖失利權而得節旄，故反謀亦未發。

translations.literal: Though Qi lost profit rights he gained the command seal, and therefore his rebellion plot had not yet surfaced.
translations.idiomatic: Qi lost revenue power but gained a command seal, and his plot had not yet surfaced.

sentences.zh: 戊子，名徐州軍曰武寧，以張愔為節度使。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Xuzhou army was named Wuning, and Zhang Yin was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the Xuzhou army was renamed Wuning; Zhang Yin became military governor.

sentences.zh: 加彰義節度使吳少誠同平章事。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng, military governor of Zhangyi, was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyi military governor Wu Shaocheng was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以王叔文為度支、鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen was made deputy commissioner of revenue and salt-and-iron transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen was made deputy commissioner of revenue and salt transport.

sentences.zh: 先是叔文與其黨謀，得國賦在手，則可以結諸用事人，取軍士心，以固其權，又懼驟使重權，人心不服，藉杜佑雅有會計之名，位重而務自全，易可制，故先令佑主其名，而自除為副以專之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shuwen and his faction had plotted that with state revenue in hand they could bind those in power, win soldiers' hearts, and consolidate their authority; they also feared that sudden heavy power would not win hearts, and relying on Du You's reputation for accounts, his high rank and wish to preserve himself, and his ease of control, they first had You hold the title while Shuwen removed himself as deputy to monopolize it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen's faction had plotted that holding revenue would bind power-holders and win the army; fearing sudden power, they used Du You's accounting fame and caution as a figurehead while Shuwen took the deputy post to control it.

sentences.zh: 叔文雖判兩使，不以簿書為意，日夜與其黨屏人竊語，人莫測其所為。

translations.literal: Though Shuwen adjudicated both offices he paid no heed to ledgers, day and night whispering with his faction behind closed doors—no one knew what they did.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shuwen held both offices he ignored accounts, whispering with his faction day and night—none knew their designs.

sentences.zh: 以御史中丞武元衡為左庶子。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wu Yuanheng was made Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wu Yuanheng was made Left Mentor.

sentences.zh: 德宗之末，叔文之黨多為御史，元衡薄其為人，待之莽鹵。

translations.literal: At the end of Dezong's reign many of Shuwen's faction were censors; Yuanheng looked down on their conduct and treated them roughly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Dezong's reign Shuwen's men were censors; Yuanheng despised them and treated them roughly.

sentences.zh: 元衡為山陵儀仗使，劉禹錫求為判官，不許。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was director of the imperial tomb guard of honor; Liu Yuxi sought to be his aide and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng directed tomb honors; Liu Yuxi sought to be his aide and was refused.

sentences.zh: 叔文以元衡在風憲，欲使附己，使其黨誘以權利，元衡不認，由是左遷。

translations.literal: Shuwen, because Yuanheng was in the censorate and wished to win him, had his faction tempt him with power and profit; Yuanheng would not acknowledge it, and therefore was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen wanted Yuanheng in the censorate and tempted him with power; Yuanheng refused and was demoted.

sentences.zh: 元衡，平一之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was a grandson of Wu Pingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng was a grandson of Wu Pingyi.

sentences.zh: 侍御史竇群奏屯田員外郎劉禹錫挾邪亂政，不宜在朝。

translations.literal: Attendant censor Dou Qun memorialized that Field Service outer director Liu Yuxi used perverse means to disorder government and should not remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Dou Qun reported that Liu Yuxi perverted government and should leave court.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謁叔文，揖之曰：「事固有不可知者。」

translations.literal: He had also called on Shuwen and bowed, saying, "In affairs there are indeed things one cannot know."
translations.idiomatic: He had also visited Shuwen and bowed, saying, "Some things cannot be known in advance."

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: Shuwen said, "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 群曰：「去歲李實怙恩挾貴，氣蓋一時，公當此時，逡巡路旁，乃江南一吏耳。

translations.literal: Qun said, "Last year Li Shi, relying on favor and arrogating rank, overawed the age; at that time you lingered by the roadside—you were but a clerk from south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "Last year Li Shi lorded over the court; then you were but a Jiangnan clerk by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 今公一旦復據其地，安知路旁無如公者乎！」

translations.literal: Now you have suddenly regained that position—how do you know there is no one like you by the roadside!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold power again—who says no one like you waits by the road!"

sentences.zh: 其黨欲逐之，韋執誼以群素有強直名，止之。

translations.literal: His faction wished to drive Qun out, but Wei Zhiyi, because Qun had a reputation for stern integrity, stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: The faction wanted Qun expelled, but Zhiyi, respecting Qun's reputation for integrity, stopped them.

sentences.zh: 上疾久不愈，時扶御殿，群臣瞻望而已，莫有親奏對者。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was long without recovery; sometimes supported he faced the main hall, and officials could only gaze—none dared approach for direct audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness lingered; sometimes propped up he faced court, and officials could only look on—none approached for direct audience.

sentences.zh: 中外危懼，思早立太子，而王叔文之黨欲專大權，惡聞之。

translations.literal: Court and country were in peril, wishing early establishment of the crown prince, but Wang Shuwen's faction wished to monopolize great power and hated to hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: All feared for the realm and wanted a crown prince named early; Shuwen's faction, grasping for power, hated the very mention.

sentences.zh: 宦官俱文珍、劉光琦、薛盈珍等皆先朝任使舊人，疾叔文、忠言等朋黨專恣，乃啟上召翰林學士鄭絪、衛次公、李程、王涯入金鑾殿，草立太子制。

translations.literal: Eunuchs Ju Wenzhen, Liu Guangqi, Xue Yingzhen, and others—all old appointees of the previous reign—detested Shuwen, Zhongyan, and their clique's exclusive arrogance; they reported to the emperor and summoned Hanlin academicians Zheng Qun, Wei Cigong, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya to the Jinluan Hall to draft the edict establishing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Ju Wenzhen, Liu Guangqi, and Xue Yingzhen—veterans of the prior reign—hated Shuwen's clique and summoned academicians Zheng Qun, Wei Cigong, Li Cheng, and Wang Ya to Jinluan Hall to draft the heir's appointment.

sentences.zh: 時牛昭容輩以廣陵王淳英睿，惡之；

translations.literal: At the time Lady Niu and her ilk, because the Prince of Guangling Chun was clever and perceptive, detested him;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Niu's circle hated the Prince of Guangling Chun for his sharp intelligence;

sentences.zh: 絪不復請，書紙為「立嫡以長」字呈上，上頷之。

translations.literal: Qun did not ask further but wrote on paper the characters "establish the legitimate eldest" and presented them; the emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: Qun wrote "establish the eldest legitimate" and showed the emperor, who nodded.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，立淳為太子，更名純。

translations.literal: On guisi Chun was established as crown prince and renamed Chun.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Chun was made crown prince and renamed Chun.

sentences.zh: 程，神符五世孫也。

translations.literal: Cheng was a fifth-generation descendant of Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was a fifth-generation descendant of Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 賈耽以王叔文黨用事，心惡之，稱疾不出，屢乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, seeing Wang Shuwen's faction in power, detested them in his heart, claimed illness and did not go out, and repeatedly begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan, seeing Shuwen's faction in power, loathed them, feigned illness, and repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，諸宰相會食中書。

translations.literal: On dingyou all the chancellors dined together in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the chancellors dined together in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相方食，百寮無敢謁見者。

translations.literal: By precedent, while chancellors were eating, no official dared visit.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent none might visit while chancellors ate.

sentences.zh: 叔文至中書，欲與執誼計事，令直省通之，直省以舊事告，叔文怒，叱直省。

translations.literal: Shuwen came to the Secretariat wishing to consult with Zhiyi on affairs; he had the duty officer announce him; the duty officer cited precedent, and Shuwen in anger rebuked the duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen came to the Secretariat to consult Zhiyi; the duty officer cited precedent; Shuwen raged at him.

sentences.zh: 直省懼，入白。

translations.literal: The duty officer in fear entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: The frightened duty officer reported within.

sentences.zh: 執誼逡巡慚赧，竟起迎叔文，就其閤語良久。

translations.literal: Zhiyi hesitated in shame but finally rose to welcome Shuwen and spoke with him long in his private room.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi flushed with shame yet rose to welcome Shuwen and talked long in his room.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、高郢、鄭珣瑜皆停箸以待，有報者云：「叔文索飯，韋相公已與之同食閤中矣。」

translations.literal: Du You, Gao Ying, and Zheng Xunyu all stopped eating and waited; a messenger reported, "Shuwen has asked for food; Vice Chancellor Wei is already eating with him in his room."
translations.idiomatic: Du You, Gao Ying, and Zheng Xunyu waited with chopsticks stilled; word came that Shuwen was dining with Wei in his room.

sentences.zh: 佑、郢心知不可，畏叔文、執誼，莫敢出言。

translations.literal: You and Ying knew in their hearts it could not stand, but fearing Shuwen and Zhiyi, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: You and Ying knew this could not stand but feared Shuwen and Zhiyi and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜獨歎曰：「吾豈可復居此位！」

translations.literal: Xunyu alone sighed, "How can I still hold this office!"
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu alone sighed, "How can I remain in this post!"

sentences.zh: 顧左右，取馬徑歸，遂不起。

translations.literal: He looked to his attendants, took a horse, and went straight home; he did not return to office.
translations.idiomatic: He took a horse straight home and never returned.

sentences.zh: 二相皆天下重望，相次歸臥，叔文、執誼等益無所顧忌，遠近大懼。

translations.literal: The two chancellors were men of great renown under heaven; they successively retired ill, and Shuwen, Zhiyi, and the rest were still more unbridled—far and near were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Two chancellors of world renown retired in succession; Shuwen and Zhiyi grew bolder—and fear spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅，立皇弟諤為欽王，誠為珍王；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renyin, the emperor's younger brother E was made Prince of Qin and Cheng Prince of Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on renyin of the fourth month, younger brother E was made Prince of Qin and Cheng Prince of Zhen;

sentences.zh: 子經為郯王，緯為均王，縱為漵王，紓為莒王，綢為密王，總為郇王，約為邵王，結為宋王，緗為集王，絲求為冀王，綺為和王，絢為衡王，絲熏為會王，綰為福王，紘為撫王，緄為岳王，紳為袁王，綸為桂王，繟為翼王。

translations.literal: his sons Jing Prince of Tan, Wei Prince of Jun, Zong Prince of Xu, Shu Prince of Ju, Chou Prince of Mi, Zong Prince of Xun, Yue Prince of Shao, Jie Prince of Song, Xiang Prince of Ji, Siqiu Prince of Ji, Qi Prince of He, Xuan Prince of Heng, Xun Prince of Hui, Wan Prince of Fu, Hong Prince of Fu, Gun Prince of Yue, Shen Prince of Yuan, Lun Prince of Gui, and Chan Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: sons Jing of Tan, Wei of Jun, Zong of Xu, Shu of Ju, Chou of Mi, Zong of Xun, Yue of Shao, Jie of Song, Xiang of Ji, Siqiu of Ji, Qi of He, Xuan of Heng, Xun of Hui, Wan of Fu, Hong of Fu, Gun of Yue, Shen of Yuan, Lun of Gui, and Chan of Yi.

sentences.zh: 乙已，上御宣政殿，冊太子。

translations.literal: On yisi the emperor faced the Xuanzheng Hall and invested the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the emperor invested the crown prince at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 百官睹太子儀表，退，皆相賀，至有感泣者，中外大喜。

translations.literal: Officials saw the crown prince's bearing and withdrew all congratulating one another; some wept with feeling; court and country were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Officials saw the heir's bearing, withdrew congratulating; some wept; all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 而王叔文獨有憂色，口不敢言，但吟杜甫題《諸葛亮祠堂》詩曰：「出師未捷身先死，長使英雄淚滿襟！」

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen alone wore a worried look; he dared not speak but recited Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine: "The expedition failed before success; heroes ever since have wet their collars with tears!"
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen alone looked troubled and recited Du Fu on Zhuge Liang: "The campaign failed before victory—heroes ever since have wept!"

sentences.zh: 聞者哂之。

translations.literal: Hearers sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners sneered.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常卿杜黃裳為裴延齡所惡，留滯台閣，十年不遷，及其婿韋執誼為相，始遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Earlier Director of Imperial Sacrifices Du Huangshang had been detested by Pei Yanling, stuck in the censorate ten years without promotion; when his son-in-law Wei Zhiyi became chancellor he was at last made Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Du Huangshang, hated by Pei Yanling, had languished in the censorate ten years until son-in-law Zhiyi made him Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 黃裳勸執誼帥群臣請太子監國，執誼驚曰：「丈人甫得一官，奈何啟口議禁中事！」

translations.literal: Huangshang urged Zhiyi to lead the officials in asking the crown prince to oversee government; Zhiyi was alarmed and said, "Sir, you have just gained an office—why open your mouth on inner-palace affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang urged Zhiyi to ask the heir to oversee government; Zhiyi cried, "You just gained a post—why meddle in palace affairs!"

sentences.zh: 黃裳勃然曰：「黃裳受恩三朝，豈得以一官相買乎！」

translations.literal: Huangshang flushed with anger and said, "Huangshang received favor through three reigns—can I be bought with one office!"
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang flared: "I served three reigns—am I bought with one office!"

sentences.zh: 拂衣起出。

translations.literal: He shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: He swept out.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以給事中陸淳為太子侍讀，仍更名質。

translations.literal: On wushen Drafting Officer Lu Chun was made tutor to the crown prince and also renamed Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen drafting officer Lu Chun became the heir's tutor and was renamed Zhi.

sentences.zh: 韋執誼自以專權，恐太子不悅，故以質為侍讀，使潛伺太子意，且解之。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi, confident in his monopoly of power and fearing the crown prince's displeasure, therefore made Zhi tutor to spy on the crown prince's mind and explain matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi, fearing the heir's displeasure, made Zhi tutor to spy on him and explain matters.

sentences.zh: 及質發言，太子怒曰：「陛下令先生為寡人講經義耳，何為預他事！」

translations.literal: When Zhi spoke the crown prince angrily said, "His Majesty ordered you, sir, to expound the classics for me—why meddle in other affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi spoke the heir snapped, "The emperor set you to teach me the classics—why meddle elsewhere!"

sentences.zh: 質惶懼而出。

translations.literal: Zhi fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛未，以右金吾大將軍范希朝為左、右神策京西諸城鎮行營節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on xinwei, Right Golden Guards general Fan Xichao was made commissioner of the Left and Right Shence western garrison circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinwei, Fan Xichao became commissioner of the Left and Right Shence western garrisons.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以度支郎中韓泰為其行軍司馬。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Revenue director Han Tai was made his marching army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu revenue director Han Tai became his marching supervisor.

sentences.zh: 王叔文自知為內外所憎疾，欲奪取宦官兵權以自固，籍希朝老將，使主其名，而實以泰專其事。

translations.literal: Shuwen knew he was hated within and without and wished to seize eunuch military power to secure himself; relying on the veteran Xichao to hold the title while Han Tai in fact managed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen, hated all around, sought eunuch armies for security—Xichao as figurehead, Han Tai in fact commanding.

sentences.zh: 人情不測其所為，益疑懼。

translations.literal: People could not fathom his plans and grew still more suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: None could read his plans; suspicion deepened.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以王叔文為戶部侍郎，依前充度支、鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: On xinmao Wang Shuwen was made Vice Minister of Revenue, continuing as deputy commissioner of revenue and salt transport.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Shuwen became Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping revenue and salt transport.

sentences.zh: 俱文珍等惡其專權，削去翰林之職。

translations.literal: Ju Wenzhen and the others detested his monopoly and stripped his Hanlin post.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen and others stripped his Hanlin post for his monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 叔文見制書，大驚，謂人曰：「叔文日時至此商量公事，若不得此院職事，則無因而至矣。」

translations.literal: Shuwen saw the appointment edict and was greatly alarmed, saying to others, "Day after day I have come here to discuss public affairs; without this courtyard post I have no way to enter."
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was shocked: "Without Hanlin I cannot reach the inner councils."

sentences.zh: 王伾即為疏請，不從。

translations.literal: Wang Pi at once memorialized on his behalf; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized for him; refused.

sentences.zh: 再疏，乃許三五日一入翰林，去學士名。

translations.literal: A second memorial was granted entry to Hanlin every three to five days, dropping the academician title.
translations.idiomatic: A second memorial won entry every few days, without the academician title.

sentences.zh: 叔文始懼。

translations.literal: Shuwen began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen began to fear.

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥，貶宣歙巡官羊士諤為汀州寧化尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jihai, Yang Shizhi, patrol officer of Xuan and She, was demoted to assistant magistrate of Ninghua in Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jihai, Xuan-She patrol officer Yang Shizhi was demoted to Ninghua assistant in Ting.

sentences.zh: 士諤以公事至長安，遇叔文用事，公言其非。

translations.literal: Shizhi had come to Chang'an on public business, encountered Shuwen in power, and openly denounced his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi came to Chang'an on business, found Shuwen in power, and denounced him openly.

sentences.zh: 叔文聞之，怒，欲下詔斬之，執誼不可；

translations.literal: When Shuwen heard he was angry and wished to issue an edict beheading him; Zhiyi would not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen wanted him beheaded by edict; Zhiyi refused;

sentences.zh: 則令杖殺之，執誼又以為不可，遂貶焉。

translations.literal: then wished to have him clubbed to death; Zhiyi again would not agree, and he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: then clubbed to death; Zhiyi refused again; he was demoted instead.

sentences.zh: 由是叔文始大惡執誼，往來二人門下者皆懼。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuwen began to hate Zhiyi greatly, and those who came and went at both men's gates were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen then hated Zhiyi; clients at both doors trembled.

sentences.zh: 先時，劉闢以劍南支度副使將韋皋之意於叔文，求都領劍南三川，謂叔文曰：「太尉使闢致微誠於公，若與某三川，當以死相助；

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Pi, as Sichuan branch revenue deputy representing Wei Gao's intent to Shuwen, asked to command all three circuits of Jiannan and said to Shuwen, "The Grand Marshal sends Pi to offer his slight sincerity to you; if you grant me the three circuits I will aid you unto death;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Pi, as Sichuan deputy for Wei Gao, asked Shuwen for all Jiannan and said, "The Grand Marshal offers his loyalty; grant the three circuits and I die for you;

sentences.zh: 若不與，亦當有以相酬。」

translations.literal: if not, there will still be repayment."
translations.idiomatic: if not, there will still be repayment."

sentences.zh: 叔文怒，亦將斬之，執誼固執不可。

translations.literal: Shuwen was angry and also wished to behead him; Zhiyi firmly would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen wanted him killed; Zhiyi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 闢尚游長安未去，聞貶士諤，遂逃歸。

translations.literal: Pi had still been lingering in Chang'an; hearing of Shizhi's demotion he fled home.
translations.idiomatic: Pi still lingered in Chang'an; hearing of Shizhi's fate he fled home.

sentences.zh: 執誼初為叔文所引用，深附之，既得位，欲掩其跡，且迫於公議，故時時為異同，輒使人謝叔文曰：「非敢負約，乃欲曲成兄事耳！」

translations.literal: Zhiyi had first been promoted by Shuwen and deeply attached to him; having gained position he wished to cover his tracks and, pressed by public opinion, therefore sometimes differed, always sending word to Shuwen, "I do not dare break our pact—I only wish to complete your affair by indirect means!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi, raised by Shuwen, now wished to hide his tracks and sometimes differed, telling Shuwen, "I do not betray you—I mean to help you indirectly!"

sentences.zh: 叔文詬怒，不之信，遂成仇怨。

translations.literal: Shuwen cursed in rage and did not believe him; they became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen raged and disbelieved; they became enemies.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，韋皋上表，以為：「陛下哀毀成疾，重勞萬機，故久而未安，請權令皇太子親監庶政，俟皇躬痊癒，復歸春宮。

translations.literal: On guichou Wei Gao memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty's mourning has brought illness and again burdens you with all affairs; therefore recovery is slow. I ask that the crown prince temporarily oversee ordinary government until Your Majesty's person heals, then return power to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Wei Gao wrote that the emperor's mourning illness required the heir to oversee government until he healed.

sentences.zh: 臣位兼將相，今之所陳，乃其職分。」

translations.literal: I hold rank as general and chancellor; what I now state is my duty."
translations.idiomatic: As general and chancellor this is my duty."

sentences.zh: 又上太子箋，以為：「聖上遠法高宗，亮陰不言，委政臣下，而所付非人。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to the crown prince, saying, "The sage emulates Gaozong, observing mourning in silence and entrusting government to ministers—but those entrusted are unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the heir that the emperor emulated Gaozong in silent mourning but entrusted unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 王叔文、王伾、李忠言之徒，輒當重任，賞罰縱情，墮紀紊綱。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen, Wang Pi, Li Zhongyan, and their ilk have usurped heavy responsibility, indulging rewards and punishments, destroying discipline and disordering the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen, Pi, Zhongyan, and their ilk seized power, indulging rewards and punishments and wrecking law.

sentences.zh: 散府庫之積以賂權門。

translations.literal: They scatter treasury stores to bribe the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered treasury stores to bribe the powerful.

sentences.zh: 樹置心腹，遍於貴位；

translations.literal: They plant trusted hearts throughout exalted posts;
translations.idiomatic: They planted trusted men in high posts;

sentences.zh: 潛結左右，憂在蕭牆。

translations.literal: secretly join with inner attendants—trouble lies within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: secretly joined inner attendants—danger lay within the palace.

sentences.zh: 竊恐傾太宗盛業，危殿下家邦，願殿下即日奏聞，斥遂群小，使政出人主，則四方獲安。」

translations.literal: I fear they will overturn Taizong's flourishing enterprise and endanger Your Highness's house and state; I beg Your Highness to report at once, drive out the petty crew, and let government issue from the sovereign—then the four quarters will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: I fear they will ruin Taizong's legacy and endanger the realm; drive them out and let government issue from the throne."

sentences.zh: 皋自恃重臣，遠處西蜀，度王叔文不能動搖，遂極言其奸。

translations.literal: Gao, relying on himself as a weighty minister far off in western Shu, judged that Wang Shuwen could not shake him, and therefore spoke to the limit of their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, a weighty minister in distant Shu, judged Shuwen could not touch him and denounced the faction fully.

sentences.zh: 俄而荊南節度使裴均、河東節度使嚴綬箋表繼至，意與皋同，中外皆倚以為援，而邪黨震懼。

translations.literal: Soon Jingnan military governor Pei Jun and Hedong military governor Yan Shou sent memorials in succession with the same intent; court and country all leaned on them as support, while the evil faction trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pei Jun of Jingnan and Yan Shou of Hedong sent like memorials; all looked to them—and the faction trembled.

sentences.zh: 均，光庭之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jun was a great-grandson of Guangting.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was a great-grandson of Pei Guangting.

sentences.zh: 王叔文既以范希朝、韓泰主京西神策軍，諸宦者尚未寤。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen having made Fan Xichao and Han Tai masters of the western Shence army, the eunuchs had not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen had put Xichao and Han Tai over the western Shence; the eunuchs had not yet understood.

sentences.zh: 會邊上諸將各以狀辭中尉，且言方屬希朝。

translations.literal: When frontier generals each sent documents declining the chief army supervisor and saying they belonged to Xichao,
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals each declined the chief supervisor and said they answered to Xichao;

sentences.zh: 宦者始寤兵柄為叔文等所奪，乃大怒曰：「從其謀，吾屬必死其手。」

translations.literal: the eunuchs first realized military power had been seized by Shuwen and the rest, and in great anger said, "If we follow their plan we are sure to die at their hands."
translations.idiomatic: the eunuchs realized Shuwen had seized the armies and cried, "Follow them and we die at their hands."

sentences.zh: 密令其使歸告諸將曰：「無以兵屬人。」

translations.literal: They secretly ordered their envoys to return and tell the generals, "Do not give your troops to others."
translations.idiomatic: They secretly told the generals, "Give your troops to no one."

sentences.zh: 希朝至奉天，諸將無至者。

translations.literal: When Xichao reached Fengtian no generals came.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao reached Fengtian; no generals came.

sentences.zh: 韓泰馳歸白之，叔文計無所出，唯曰：「奈何！

translations.literal: Han Tai galloped back to report; Shuwen had no plan and could only say, "What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Han Tai raced back to report; Shuwen had no plan—"What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 奈何！」

translations.literal: What is to be done!"
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!"

sentences.zh: 無幾，其母病甚。

translations.literal: Before long his mother's illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his mother fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，叔文盛具酒饌，與諸學士及李忠言、俱文珍、劉光琦等飲於翰林。

translations.literal: On bingchen Shuwen set out a great feast of wine and food and drank in Hanlin with the academicians, Li Zhongyan, Ju Wenzhen, Liu Guangqi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Shuwen feasted academicians, Zhongyan, Ju Wenzhen, and Liu Guangqi in Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 叔文言曰：「叔文母病，以身任國事之故，不得親醫藥，今將求假歸侍。

translations.literal: Shuwen said, "Shuwen's mother is ill; because I bear state affairs in person I cannot attend her with medicine—now I will ask leave to go home and serve her.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen said his mother was ill; bearing state affairs he could not nurse her and would ask leave.

sentences.zh: 叔文比竭心力，不避危難，皆為朝廷之恩。

translations.literal: Shuwen has lately exhausted his strength, not avoiding danger and difficulty—all for the court's grace.
translations.idiomatic: He had exhausted himself in the court's service.

sentences.zh: 一旦去歸，百謗交至，誰肯見察以一言相助乎？」

translations.literal: Once I leave, a hundred slanders will converge—who will see clearly enough to help me with a word?"
translations.idiomatic: Once I leave, slanders will converge—who will speak for me?"

sentences.zh: 文珍隨其語輒折之，叔文不能對，但引滿相勸，酒數行而罷。

translations.literal: Wenzhen answered every phrase with a rebuttal; Shuwen could not reply but only urged full cups in toasting; after several rounds of wine they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen rebutted every line; Shuwen could only toast; after several rounds they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，叔文以母喪去位。

translations.literal: On dingsi Shuwen left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Shuwen left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙子，加李師古檢校侍中。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingzi, Li Shigu was made acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on bingzi of the seventh month, Li Shigu was made acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王叔文既有母喪，韋執誼益不用其語。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen having entered mourning for his mother, Wei Zhiyi paid still less heed to his words.
translations.idiomatic: With Shuwen in mourning, Zhiyi heeded him even less.

sentences.zh: 叔文怒，與其黨日夜謀起復，必先斬執誼而盡誅不附己者，聞者忷懼。

translations.literal: Shuwen was angry; day and night he and his faction plotted his return to office, first to behead Zhiyi and execute all who did not follow him—hearers were alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen raged and plotted return—first beheading Zhiyi and all who opposed him.

sentences.zh: 自叔文歸第，王伾失據，日詣宦官及杜佑請起叔文為相，且總北軍；

translations.literal: From the time Shuwen returned home Wang Pi lost his footing, daily visiting eunuchs and Du You to ask that Shuwen be made chancellor and also command the northern armies;
translations.idiomatic: Pi lost footing and daily begged eunuchs and Du You to restore Shuwen as chancellor and northern commander;

sentences.zh: 既不獲，則請以為威遠軍使、平章事，又不得。

translations.literal: when that failed he asked that Shuwen be made commissioner of the Weiyuan army and Grand Councillor—again denied.
translations.idiomatic: failing that he asked Weiyuan commissioner and Grand Councillor—again denied.

sentences.zh: 其黨皆憂悸不自保。

translations.literal: His faction were all anxious and could not preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The faction could not preserve themselves.

sentences.zh: 是日，伾坐翰林中，疏三上，不報，知事不濟，行且臥，至夜，忽叫曰：「伾中風矣！」

translations.literal: That day Pi sat in Hanlin, memorializing thrice without answer; knowing affairs would not succeed he was about to lie down when at night he suddenly cried, "Pi has had a stroke!"
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized thrice from Hanlin without answer; at night he cried, "Pi has had a stroke!"

sentences.zh: 明日，遂輿歸不出。

translations.literal: The next day he was carried home in a litter and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was carried home and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以倉部郎中、判度支案陳諫為河中少尹。

translations.literal: On jichou Chen Jian, director of the Revenue Bureau, was made junior vice-prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou revenue bureau director Chen Jian was made Hezhong junior vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 伾、叔文之黨至是始去。

translations.literal: Pi and Shuwen's faction at last departed.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and Shuwen's faction at last fell.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，橫海軍節度使程懷信薨，以其子副使執恭為留後。

translations.literal: On guisi Henghai military governor Cheng Huaixin died; his son acting commissioner Zhigong was made acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Henghai governor Cheng Huaixin died; son Zhigong became acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 乙未，制以「積疢未復，其軍國政事，權令皇太子純句當。」

translations.literal: On yiwei an edict said, "Illness long unhealed; military and civil government is temporarily entrusted to the crown prince Chun."
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei an edict entrusted military and civil affairs to Crown Prince Chun.

sentences.zh: 時內外共疾王叔文黨與專恣，上亦惡之。

translations.literal: At the time within and without all detested Wang Shuwen's faction's exclusive arrogance; the emperor also hated them.
translations.idiomatic: All hated Shuwen's faction; the emperor too.

sentences.zh: 俱文珍等屢啟上請令太子監國，上固厭倦萬機，遂許之。

translations.literal: Ju Wenzhen and the others repeatedly reported asking the crown prince to oversee government; the emperor, weary of all affairs, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen repeatedly asked the heir to govern; the weary emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又以太常卿杜黃裳為門下侍郎，左金吾大將軍袁滋為中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang was also made Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat, and Left Golden Guards general Yuan Zi Vice Grand Councillor—both Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang and Left Golden Guards Yuan Zi became Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 俱文珍等以其舊臣，故引用之。

translations.literal: Ju Wenzhen and the others, because they were old ministers, therefore promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs promoted them as old ministers.

sentences.zh: 又以鄭珣瑜為吏部尚書，高郢為刑部尚書，並罷政事。

translations.literal: Zheng Xunyu was also made Minister of Personnel and Gao Ying Minister of Justice—both removed from government.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xunyu became Minister of Personnel and Gao Ying Minister of Justice—both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 太子見百官於東朝堂，百官拜賀。

translations.literal: The crown prince received officials in the Eastern Court; officials bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: The heir received officials in the Eastern Court; they congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 太子涕泣，不答拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince wept and did not return the bows.
translations.idiomatic: The heir wept and did not return the bows.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚子，制「令太子即皇帝位，朕稱太上皇，制敕稱誥。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengzi, an edict said, "Let the crown prince immediately take the imperial throne; I shall be styled Retired Emperor; edicts and appointments shall be called proclamations."
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict declared the crown prince emperor, the retired sovereign styled Retired Emperor, and edicts renamed proclamations.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太上皇徙居興慶宮，誥改元永貞，立良娣王氏為太上皇后。

translations.literal: On xinchou the Retired Emperor moved to Xingqing Palace; the proclamation changed the era name to Yongzhen and made Lady of Good Virtue Wang Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the Retired Emperor moved to Xingqing Palace, proclaimed Yongzhen, and made Lady Wang Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 後，憲宗之母也。

translations.literal: The empress was the mother of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: She was Xianzong's mother.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，貶王伾開州司馬、王叔文渝州司戶。

translations.literal: On renyin Wang Pi was demoted to army supervisor of Kai Prefecture and Wang Shuwen to household registrar of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Pi was demoted to Kai army supervisor and Shuwen to Yu household registrar.

sentences.zh: 伾尋病死貶所。

translations.literal: Before long Pi died of illness at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Pi soon died in exile.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜叔文死。

translations.literal: The next year Shuwen was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shuwen was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，憲宗即位於宣政殿。

translations.literal: On yisi Xianzong took the throne in the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Xianzong ascended at Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙午，昇平公主獻女口五十。

translations.literal: On bingwu Princess Shengping presented fifty women.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Princess Shengping offered fifty women.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「上皇不受獻，朕何敢違！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Retired Emperor does not accept presentations—how dare I disobey!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Retired Emperor refuses gifts—how dare I accept!"

sentences.zh: 遂卻之。

translations.literal: He thereupon declined them.
translations.idiomatic: He declined them.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，荊南獻毛龜二，上曰：「聯所寶惟賢。

translations.literal: On gengxu Jingnan presented two hairy tortoises; the emperor said, "What I treasure is the worthy alone.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Jingnan sent two hairy tortoises; the emperor said, "I treasure only the worthy.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾、神芝，皆虛美耳，所以《春秋》不書祥瑞。

translations.literal: Fine grain and divine fungus are all empty praise; therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: Fine grain and divine fungus are empty flattery—the Spring and Autumn Annals records no omens.

sentences.zh: 自今凡有嘉瑞，但准令申有司，勿復以聞。

translations.literal: Henceforth whenever there are auspicious signs, merely report them to the relevant office as regulations require; do not again report them to me.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter report omens only to the proper office, not to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及珍禽奇獸，皆毋得獻。」

translations.literal: Rare birds and strange beasts likewise may not be presented."
translations.idiomatic: Rare birds and beasts may not be presented either."

sentences.zh: 癸丑，西川節度使南康忠武王韋皋薨。

translations.literal: On guichou Wei Gao, military governor of western Shu, Prince of Nankang and Loyal Martial King, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou western Shu military governor Wei Gao, Prince of Nankang, died.

sentences.zh: 皋在蜀二十一年，重加賦斂，豐貢獻以結主恩，厚給賜以撫士卒。

translations.literal: Gao had been in Shu twenty-one years, repeatedly increasing levies, enriching tribute to bind imperial favor, and generously bestowing gifts to comfort the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ruled Shu twenty-one years, raising levies, enriching tribute to court the throne, and generously paying the troops.

sentences.zh: 士卒婚嫁死喪，皆供其資費，以是得久安其位而士卒樂為之用，服南詔，摧吐蕃。

translations.literal: For soldiers' weddings, funerals, and deaths he supplied expenses, and thereby held his post long in peace while the troops gladly served him; he subdued Nanzhao and crushed Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He paid soldiers' wedding and funeral costs, held power long, won their loyalty, subdued Nanzhao, and crushed Tibet.

sentences.zh: 幕僚歲久官崇者則為刺史，已復還幕府，終不使還朝，恐洩其所為故也。

translations.literal: Staff who had served many years and risen high became prefects, then returned again to the headquarters—never sent back to court, lest they reveal what he had done.
translations.idiomatic: Long-serving staff became prefects then returned to his staff—never sent to court lest they reveal his deeds.

sentences.zh: 府庫既實，時寬其民，三年一復租賦，蜀人服其智謀而畏其威，至今畫像以為土神，家家祀之。

translations.literal: The treasury being full, he sometimes eased the people, restoring rent and tax every three years; the people of Shu admired his stratagems and feared his might, and to this day his image is painted as a local god and every household sacrifices to him.
translations.idiomatic: With full treasuries he eased the people every three years; Shu feared his power and still paints him a local god in every home.

sentences.zh: 支度副使劉闢自為留後。

translations.literal: Branch revenue deputy Liu Pi made himself acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue deputy Liu Pi made himself acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 郎州武陵、龍陽江漲，流萬餘家。

translations.literal: In Lang Prefecture the Wu and Longyang rivers rose and swept away more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Lang the Wu and Longyang rivers flooded more than ten thousand households away.

sentences.zh: 壬午，奉義節度使伊慎入朝。

translations.literal: On renwu Fengyi military governor Yi Shen entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Fengyi military governor Yi Shen came to court.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，夏綏節度使韓全義入明。

translations.literal: On xinmao Xia-Sui military governor Han Quanyi entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Xia-Sui military governor Han Quanyi came to court.

sentences.zh: 全義敗於殷水而還，不朝覲而去，上在籓邸，聞其事而惡之。

translations.literal: Quanyi had been defeated at Yinshui and returned without attending audience and left; when the emperor was still in the princely residence he heard of the matter and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi, defeated at Yinshui, had left without audience; the emperor, still a prince, had detested him.

sentences.zh: 全義懼，乃請入朝。

translations.literal: Quanyi was afraid and therefore asked to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing, Quanyi asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 劉闢使諸將表求節鉞，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Liu Pi had his generals memorialize asking for the command seal; the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's generals asked for the command seal; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 己未，以袁滋為劍南東、西川、山南西道安撫大使。

translations.literal: On jiwei Yuan Zi was made pacification commissioner of eastern and western Sichuan and southern Shannan west.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Yuan Zi was made pacification commissioner for Sichuan and southern Shannan.

sentences.zh: 度支秦裴延齡所置別庫，皆減正庫之物別貯之。

translations.literal: The separate treasuries Pei Yanling had established under the Revenue Bureau all stored items taken from the main treasury separately.
translations.idiomatic: Separate treasuries Yanling had set under Revenue held goods diverted from the main store.

sentences.zh: 請並歸正庫，從之。

translations.literal: A request that they all be returned to the main treasury was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They were merged back into the main treasury.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遣度支、鹽鐵轉運副使潘孟陽宣慰江、淮，行視租賦、榷稅利害，因察官史否臧，百姓疾苦。

translations.literal: On xinyou deputy commissioner of revenue and salt transport Pan Mengyang was sent to comfort Jiang and Huai, inspect the benefits and harms of rent and monopoly taxes, and also investigate officials' right and wrong and the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou revenue deputy Pan Mengyang was sent to comfort Jiang-Huai, inspect taxes, and investigate officials and popular hardship.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以尚書左丞鄭餘慶同平章事。

translations.literal: On guihai Zheng Yuqing, Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Left Vice Minister Zheng Yuqing became Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊辰，禮儀使奏：「曾太皇太皇沈氏歲月滋深，迎訪理絕。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuchen, the director of rites memorialized, "Great-great-grandmother Empress Shen's years grow ever deeper and search and reception are logically ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rites director reported that Empress Shen's years made further search impossible.

sentences.zh: 案晉庾蔚之議，尋求三年之外，俟中壽而服之。

translations.literal: According to the discussion of Yu Weizhi of Jin, after three years of search one waits until middle age to don mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Following Jin scholar Yu Weizhi, after three years one waits until middle age to mourn.

sentences.zh: 伏請以大行皇帝啟攢宮日，皇帝帥百官舉哀，即以其日為忌。」

translations.literal: I ask that on the day the late emperor's coffin left the palace the emperor lead the officials in mourning and take that day as the anniversary of death."
translations.idiomatic: Let the day the late emperor's coffin left the palace be the mourning day and anniversary."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 壬申，監修國史韋執誼奏，始令史官撰《日曆》。

translations.literal: On renshen Wei Zhiyi, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, memorialized that historians were for the first time ordered to compile the Daily Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen national history supervisor Wei Zhiyi ordered historians to compile the Daily Calendar.

sentences.zh: 己卯，貶神策行軍司馬韓泰為撫州刺史，司封郎中韓曄為池州刺史，禮部員外郎柳宗元為邵州刺史，屯田員外郎劉禹錫為連州刺史。

translations.literal: On jimao Shence marching supervisor Han Tai was demoted to prefect of Fu Prefecture, Personnel director Han Ye to Chi Prefecture, Rites outer director Liu Zongyuan to Shao Prefecture, and Field Service outer director Liu Yuxi to Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Han Tai became Fu prefect, Han Ye Chi prefect, Liu Zongyuan Shao prefect, and Liu Yuxi Lian prefect.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，右僕射、同平章事賈耽薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou Right Vice Minister and Grand Councillor Jia Dan died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on dingyou Grand Councillor Jia Dan died.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以中書侍郎、同平章事袁滋同平章事，充西川節度使；

translations.literal: On wuxu Vice Grand Councillor Yuan Zi was made Grand Councillor and military governor of western Shu;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Yuan Zi became Grand Councillor and western Shu military governor;

sentences.zh: 征劉闢為給事中。

translations.literal: Liu Pi was summoned as drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi was summoned as drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 舒王誼薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Shu Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Yi died.

sentences.zh: 太常議曾太皇太后謚曰睿真皇后。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title of Empress Ruizhen for the great-great-grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous title Empress Ruizhen.

sentences.zh: 山人羅令則自長安如普潤，矯稱太上皇誥，徵兵於秦州刺史劉澭，且說澭以廢立。

translations.literal: The mountain man Luo Lingze, going from Chang'an to Pujun, falsely claimed a proclamation of the Retired Emperor to raise troops from Qin Prefecture military governor Liu Yong, and also urged Yong on deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain man Luo Lingze forged a Retired Emperor proclamation to raise Qin governor Liu Yong in deposition and enthronement.

sentences.zh: 澭執送長安，並其黨杖殺之。

translations.literal: Yong seized him and sent him to Chang'an; he and his faction were clubbed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent him to Chang'an; he and his party were clubbed to death.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬神武孝文皇帝於崇陵，廟號德宗。

translations.literal: On jiyou the Divine Martial and Filial Cultured Emperor was buried at Chongling; temple name Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Dezong was buried at Chongling.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己巳，祔睿真皇后、德宗皇帝主於太廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jisi, tablets for Empress Ruizhen and Emperor Dezong were enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month tablets for Empress Ruizhen and Dezong entered the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使杜黃裳等議，以為：「國家法周制，太祖猶後稷，高祖猶文王，太宗猶武王，皆不遷。

translations.literal: Rites director Du Huangshang and others discussed, holding that the state follows Zhou institutions: the founding ancestor corresponds to Hou Ji, Gaozu to King Wen, Taizong to King Wu—all unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang argued the state followed Zhou: founding ancestor, Gaozu, and Taizong remain unmoved.

sentences.zh: 高宗在三昭三穆之外，請遷主於西夾室。」

translations.literal: Gaozong lies outside the three zhao and three mu; I ask that his tablet be moved to the western side chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong lies outside the three zhao and three mu; move his tablet to the western side chamber."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 壬申，貶中書侍郎、同平章事韋執誼為崖州司馬。

translations.literal: On renshen Vice Grand Councillor Wei Zhiyi was demoted to army supervisor of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Wei Zhiyi was demoted to Ya army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 執誼以嘗與王叔文異同，且杜黃裳婿，故獨後貶。

translations.literal: Zhiyi had once differed with Wang Shuwen and was son-in-law to Du Huangshang; therefore he alone was demoted late.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had differed with Shuwen and was Huangshang's son-in-law, Zhiyi was demoted last.

sentences.zh: 然叔文敗，執誼亦自失形勢，知禍且至，雖尚為相，常不自得，奄奄無氣，聞人行聲，輒惶悸失色，以至於貶。

translations.literal: Yet when Shuwen failed, Zhiyi also lost his footing, knowing disaster was coming; though still chancellor he was constantly ill at ease, feeble and breathless; hearing people's footsteps he would start in terror and change color—until his demotion.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuwen's fall Zhiyi, still chancellor, lived in terror until demoted.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以韓全義為太子少保，致仕。

translations.literal: On wuyin Han Quanyi was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Han Quanyi was made Junior Tutor and retired.

sentences.zh: 劉闢不受征，阻兵自守。

translations.literal: Liu Pi did not accept the summons and blocked troops in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Pi refused the summons and held troops.

sentences.zh: 袁滋畏其強，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yuan Zi feared his strength and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi feared him and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 上怒，貶滋為吉州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Zi to prefect of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Zi to Ji prefect.

sentences.zh: 復以右庶子武元衡為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng was again made Right Mentor and censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng was again made Right Mentor and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 朝議謂王叔文之黨或自員外郎出為刺史，貶之太輕。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Wang Shuwen's faction, sent from outer directors to be prefects, were demoted too lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held Shuwen's men, demoted from outer director to prefect, were punished too lightly.

sentences.zh: 己卯，再貶韓泰為虔州司馬、韓曄為饒州司馬、柳宗元為永州司馬、劉禹錫為朗州司馬，又貶河中少尹陳諫為台州司馬，和州刺史凌准為連州司馬，岳州刺史程異為郴州司馬。

translations.literal: On jimao they were demoted again: Han Tai to Qian army supervisor, Han Ye to Rao army supervisor, Liu Zongyuan to Yong army supervisor, Liu Yuxi to Lang army supervisor; also Hezhong junior vice-prefect Chen Jian to Tai army supervisor, He prefect Ling Zhun to Lian army supervisor, and Yue prefect Cheng Yi to Chen army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao they were demoted again to army supervisors: Han Tai to Qian, Han Ye to Rao, Liu Zongyuan to Yong, Liu Yuxi to Lang, Chen Jian to Tai, Ling Zhun to Lian, and Cheng Yi to Chen.

sentences.zh: 回鶻懷信可汗卒，遣鴻臚少卿孫杲臨吊，冊其嗣為騰裡野合俱錄毘伽可汗。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Creditable Khan died; Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Sun Gao was sent to mourn and invest the successor as Tengliye Kaghan.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur Creditable Khan died; Sun Gao mourned and invested his successor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，加山南東道節度使于頔同平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, southern Shannan east military governor Yu Di was made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yu Di of southern Shannan east was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以奉義節度使伊慎為右僕射。

translations.literal: Fengyi military governor Yi Shen was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi military governor Yi Shen was made Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以給事中劉闢為西川節度副使、知節度事。

translations.literal: On jiyou drafting officer Liu Pi was made deputy military governor of western Shu and acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Liu Pi was made western Shu deputy and acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 上以初嗣位，力未能計故也。

translations.literal: The emperor, having just succeeded to the throne, lacked strength to act and therefore yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor, not yet strong enough to act, yielded.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫韋丹上疏，以為：「今釋闢不誅，則朝廷可以指臂而使者，惟兩京耳。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Censor Wei Dan memorialized, holding that, "If Pi is released unpunished, then of those the court can move at a gesture, only the two capitals remain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan wrote that sparing Pi meant only the two capitals would obey the court.

sentences.zh: 此外誰不為叛！」

translations.literal: Beyond that, who will not rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Who beyond them would not rebel!"

sentences.zh: 上善其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以丹為東川節度使。

translations.literal: On renzi Wei Dan was made military governor of eastern Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Wei Dan was made eastern Chuan military governor.

sentences.zh: 丹，津之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was a fifth-generation descendant of Wei Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was a fifth-generation descendant of Wei Jin.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，百官請上上皇尊號曰應乾聖壽太上皇，上尊號曰文武大聖孝德皇帝。

translations.literal: On xinyou officials asked to give the Retired Emperor the honorific Responding to Heaven, Sagely Longevity Retired Emperor, and the emperor the honorific Civil and Martial, Great Sage, Filial and Virtuous Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou officials proposed honorifics for Retired Emperor and emperor.

sentences.zh: 上許上上皇尊號而自辭不受。

translations.literal: The emperor granted the Retired Emperor's honorific but declined his own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the Retired Emperor's title but declined his own.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以翰林學士鄭絪為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On renxu Hanlin academician Zheng Qun was made Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Hanlin academician Zheng Qun became Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以刑部郎中杜兼為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice director Du Jian was made prefect of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Justice director Du Jian was made Su prefect.

sentences.zh: 兼辭行，上書稱李錡且反，必奏族臣。

translations.literal: Jian declined to go and memorialized that Li Qi was about to rebel and would surely have his clan executed upon report.
translations.idiomatic: Jian declined, warning that Li Qi would rebel and destroy his clan if he went.

sentences.zh: 上然之，留為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and kept him as Personnel director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and kept him at Personnel.
